fl-doctor 0.1.0 — User guide

Introduction

What it is and what it answers

fl-doctor is a terminal tool that diagnoses Illumio FlowLink on the same machine where it runs (the collector). It is a single static Linux binary with no dependencies. It has a terminal UI (TUI) for day-to-day work and headless subcommands for scripts and monitoring.

This guide is written for the person who runs the FlowLink collector and for pre-sales and engineering colleagues who accompany a rollout. You do not need to know FlowLink internals.

When a switch or router exports flows to FlowLink and the PCE map does not show the expected servers, the break can be at any of five links. Without a tool, finding it takes hours of tcpdump, tshark, log reading and back-and-forth with the Illumio FlowLink user. fl-doctor answers, in minutes:

  1. Are flows reaching the collector (NetFlow, IPFIX, sFlow, text), and from which switch or router?
  2. Does a specific IP show up inside those flows?
  3. Does FlowLink receive them, process them and upload them to the PCE?
  4. Which IPs did the collector see, and which of them does FlowLink report?
  5. If something fails, what evidence do you send to support?

It is used in two ways:

ModeHow to open itWhat for
Interface (TUI)sudo fl-doctorExplore, follow an IP, build evidence. Seven tabs.
Headless (CLI)sudo fl-doctor health, trace, top, log, evidence…Scripts, cron, monitoring, JSON or CSV output.

Four field failures

Four real cases from the field (anonymized) show why a tool like this is needed:

  • FlowLink was running and processing hundreds of thousands of flows per cycle, but never uploaded anything to the PCE: the collector could not resolve the PCE's DNS name. The log showed the error on every attempt, but nobody had read it. fl-doctor shows it in 5 FlowLink › Log (indicators L11 and L12) and in the PCE exit test on 6 Host.
  • Millions of flows discarded as "bad data" in the log. They were 100% ICMP, not a data problem. fl-doctor breaks the discards down by protocol in 5 FlowLink › Log.
  • The exporter was sending flows, but from a point in the network that does not see the server segment. The IPs being looked for never appeared, even though everything else worked. fl-doctor exposes it with the IP ladder (rung N0) and the exporter's sampling.
  • A switch exported to a UDP port FlowLink was not listening on. The packets reached the collector and the kernel dropped them silently. fl-doctor flags it in 2 Exporters (FlowLink column: no listener) and in the chain (check B2).

What it does and what it does not

  • Read-only. It does not restart FlowLink, change its configuration, or touch the firewall, routes or sysctl. It writes only to its own output folder (/var/tmp/fl-doctor/) and to its preferences.
  • It does not take packets away from FlowLink. It copies traffic with AF_PACKET, the same mechanism tcpdump uses. It never opens the collector's ports, since that would split the datagrams between two processes.
  • It sends nothing out and has no telemetry. The one exception is an optional reachability test to the PCE (DNS, proxy, TLS and node_available) at the address in FlowLink's config.yaml. It carries no credentials. Turn it off with --offline.
  • Secrets stay hidden. FlowLink's API key is never shown or written. In the evidence package, the values of sensitive configuration keys are replaced with <oculto> (hidden). If the YAML cannot be parsed, the configuration is left out and the package says so. What you copy with y goes through the same redactor.
  • It does not store traffic "just in case". It reads each datagram once, updates counters and drops it. It writes traffic to disk only when you ask for it (disk capture, dedicated capture or black box).
  • Light on CPU and memory. It lowers its own priority (nice 10) and has a fixed memory budget (see "Memory and performance"). Measured on a Rocky 9 x86_64 virtual machine, replaying a real NetStream capture for 5 minutes: the normal profile holds at about 22 MB, with a brief peak of up to about 33 MB right after startup (inside its 64 MB budget), and the lean profile at about 14 MB (32 MB budget), flat over time. An IPFIX file with 199,569 records decoded to the same result as tshark.
  • It does not query the PCE with credentials. What happens inside the PCE is out of scope. fl-doctor goes as far as FlowLink's log ("cycle delivered, response 204") and records that context in the evidence for support.
Important: sudo fl-doctor is equivalent to root. Its path options (--profile, --config, --patterns, --file, --flowlink-exe, --flowlink-user) make fl-doctor read, as root, files chosen by whoever invokes it, and part of the content is displayed. Do not grant it in sudoers to accounts that should not have root. If you need a restricted sudo, restrict the arguments in sudoers, not in fl-doctor.

Unofficial tool

Important: fl-doctor is an unofficial tool, provided "as is", with no warranty and no Illumio support. It is not an Illumio product and Illumio does not endorse it. Use it with judgement and validate its results before making decisions in production.

fl-doctor is meant to help the operator and colleagues reach the cause of a break faster, and to make the evidence package useful input when you consult whoever is appropriate about FlowLink. The facts about FlowLink quoted in this guide come from Illumio's official documentation (see "Sources"); what describes how fl-doctor works comes from its own manual and its own measurements.

Installation and first use

Requirements

SystemLinux x86_64 or aarch64. The binary is static and needs no libraries. FlowLink 2.0.0 documentation lists "CentOS or RHEL server" as its platform (see "Sources").
Privilegesroot or sudo, to capture traffic and read FlowLink's files. Without root it works with whatever it can read (degraded mode, with a warning).
Terminal80×24 minimum. UTF-8 recommended; if symbols look wrong, the UI falls back to ASCII.
Optionaltshark, tcpdump or dumpcap: only for the commands fl-doctor prepares for you and for long captures to disk.
DiskAn output folder (/var/tmp/fl-doctor/ by default) with room for the evidence packages and the captures you ask for.

Verify and install

sha256sum -c SHA256SUMS                                     # verify the download
sudo install -m 0755 fl-doctor-0.1.0-x86_64-linux /usr/local/bin/fl-doctor
fl-doctor --version
sudo /usr/local/bin/fl-doctor selftest                      # check the platform

Use the checksum file that ships with the release. Release 0.1.0 ships with SHA-256 sums and a software bill of materials (SBOM). It is not signed: verify against the checksum.

Important: On RHEL and derivatives, sudo does not search /usr/local/bin (secure_path). Use the full path, sudo /usr/local/bin/fl-doctor, or start a shell with sudo -i and type fl-doctor. In this guide, sudo fl-doctor stands for either form.

Platform self-test (selftest)

selftest uses neither the network nor FlowLink and needs root (it uses AF_PACKET). It starts a fake collector on the lo interface, sends it synthetic flows, and checks that fl-doctor decodes all of them without taking any away from the collector, that the memory budget is respected and that an evidence package can be built. The disk-capture check needs tcpdump or dumpcap.

How to run it

  1. Run sudo /usr/local/bin/fl-doctor selftest (add --output DIR to choose where the result is left).
  2. Wait for the final summary.

Expected result: the last line says SELF-TEST: OK (in Spanish, AUTOPRUEBA: OK), followed by FL-DOCTOR-RESULT … command=selftest … result=ok and exit code 0. It leaves a .json and a .tgz (fl-doctor-selftest-<architecture>-<date>-<time>.tgz) with permissions 600 and nobody's data: send them back only if something fails.

Try the interface with demo

fl-doctor demo opens the interface with built-in synthetic exporters. It needs no root, network or FlowLink. It is useful for getting to know the screens and keys before opening the tool on a real collector. Without a terminal (for example redirected to a file) it prints the screens as text.

First start

The first time you open sudo fl-doctor, a three-step assistant appears (you can skip it with Esc; the defaults stay and it does not ask again):

StepWhat it asksKeys
1 of 3Do the symbols ┌─┐ ▁▅█ ✓ look right in your terminal?⏎ or s/y = yes; n = no (uses ASCII)
2 of 3Theme (auto, brand, terminal, light, mono)← → to preview each one, ⏎ next
3 of 3Language (Spanish or English)← →, ⏎ finishes

Then a five-step tour follows (Home, following an IP, who sends what, evidence, palette/help/settings). Navigate with ← → or ⏎, close with Esc, and reopen it any time with :tutor in the command palette.

If something looks wrong, fl-doctor doctor diagnoses the terminal (size, UTF-8, color, glyphs, clipboard) and tells you which preference files it uses.

The interface

Anatomy of the screen

 fl-doctor 0.1.0 · colector-01 · FlowLink ✓ 2.0.0 · capture ✓ native ens192 · 15m · ● LIVE      14:32:05 UTC
 1 Home  2 Exporters  3 IPs  4 Flows  5 FlowLink  6 Host  7 Capture                                   ES/EN
 …body: one or more panels…
 Home › Chain › B Host         ⏎ details  r trace IP  e evidence  space watch  p pause  ←→ tabs  Tab panel  ? help

Names (tabs, columns, panels, filters, actions) are always in English, also with the interface in Spanish. What explains things (descriptions, warnings, next steps, help) follows the chosen language: L, --lang es|en, or the saved language.

Header

A single line, left to right. On a narrow terminal the least important parts are hidden first; the version, the LIVE/FROZEN state and (under memory pressure) the memory indicator are never hidden.

PartWhat it shows
fl-doctor 0.1.0Tool version.
colector-01Name of the host it runs on.
FlowLink ✓ 2.0.0State of the FlowLink service (symbol) and its version.
capture ✓ native ens192Capture engine (auto, native, tcpdump, dumpcap) and interface; with several, "2 interfaces". When reading a file it says file.
15mTime window of the screens (1m, 5m, 15m, 1h or ∞ = since opening).
filter: …Only appears when a global filter is active.
mem ● 41/64 MB · system 2.1 GB free · window 30mMemory fl-doctor uses against its budget, free memory on the host and statistics window. At critical level it adds sampled 1:N. See "Memory and performance".
rec ● used/capOnly while a disk capture or the black box is running.
cpu N%fl-doctor's own CPU use.
● LIVE / ■ FROZEN hh:mm:ss / FILELive, paused since that time, or reading a file.
14:32:05 UTCCollector time. All times are shown in UTC.

Tabs and bottom bar

The second line holds the seven numbered tabs and, on the right, ES/EN (active language highlighted). The last line is the bottom bar: breadcrumbs on the left (for example Home › Chain › B Host) and the focused panel's key hints on the right. It always ends with ←→ tabs · Tab panel · ? help. With the preference barra = "minima" it shows a single hint.

Panels, focus and rows

  • The focused panel has a thick border and ● in its title. Tab and Shift-Tab switch panels in views that have more than one (Home, IPs › Watched, Flows › Ranking, FlowLink › Log, Capture).
  • The selected row carries ▶. If a cell's text does not fit, the selected row expands below it (↳) and the rest ends in ….
  • Watched IPs carry ◆ next to the IP and a ▌ bar on the left in every view.
  • The selection position is remembered in each tab.
  • The layout adapts to the width: under 120 columns, one column; 120 to 159, two; 160 and up, three. Below 80×24 only a notice to enlarge the terminal is shown.

States and symbols

Status never relies on color alone. Each one has a symbol and a word:

SymbolASCIIMeaning
✓[OK]OK
▲[!!]Warning
✗[XX]Failure
·[--]Information
?[--]No data (cannot be judged yet)
≈—Approximate figure (see "Reference by tab › 4 Flows")
● ▲ ✗ in mem—Memory level: normal, attention, critical

Screen sizes and layout

The body adapts to the terminal. The same tab is arranged differently depending on the width:

TerminalWhat you get
160 columns or moreUp to three columns. Home shows Chain, Funnel and Log indicators side by side.
120 to 159 columnsTwo columns. Home drops the Log indicators panel (they are still in 5 FlowLink › Log).
80 to 119 columnsOne column: panels are stacked, tables hide their lowest-priority columns and the header drops its least important parts.
Less than 80×24Nothing but a notice: "Enlarge the terminal: minimum 80×24, now 60×18" (with your real size).

In a table, the first column always stays; when the others do not fit, the ones with the lowest priority are hidden first. Shift-← Shift-→ (or < >) slide the table sideways so you can reach the hidden ones (a ◀ +N mark at the bottom of the panel tells how many columns are scrolled out).

Note: The screens of this section come from fl-doctor demo (synthetic data and a simulated FlowLink); see "About the screenshots and the example data" in the Introduction. In demo the FlowLink service shows ✗ in the header because no real FlowLink is running; on a real collector it shows the real state.

Details, enlarge and pause

  • Detail (⏎). Opens a window with everything about the row: for a chain link, what was checked, where the datum came from (capture, kernel, configuration, log or inference) and the suggested next step; for a Live record, all the template fields; for a log indicator, its explanation. For link E (PCE) it says it is outside the collector.
  • Enlarge (z). Makes the focused panel fill the whole body. Esc or z go back.
  • Pause (p). Freezes the screens so you can read without them moving (the header shows ■ FROZEN with the time). Captures and counters keep running underneath; when you follow again, the next snapshot replaces the frozen one.
  • Window (t, +, -). Chooses which part of the statistics you see. It never exceeds the memory profile's statistics window.

Which detail windows exist

⏎ opens a different window depending on the row. All of them scroll with ↑ ↓, copy their text with y and close with Esc or ⏎.

Where you press ⏎Window titleWhat it shows
1 Home › ChainLink A · Exporters (A to E)Every check of the link: symbol, id (A1…), title and the origin of the datum in brackets (wire, kernel, config, log, inferred), the explanation and the Next step. Link E explains that the PCE is outside the collector.
2 Exporters › Table(the panel itself is widened)The same as the right-hand panel, using the whole body.
3 IPs › SeenIP seen <ip>First seen, Last seen (with "how long ago"), Records, Exporters, FlowLink (reported / not reported / unknown) and whether it is Watched. At the bottom, the actions: space watch · C capture to disk · e evidence · r trace.
4 Flows › Ranking<ip> · breakdownFlows (with percentage), Peers, Bytes, Packets, Seen and, below, the per-exporter breakdown.
4 Flows › LiveFlow recordEvery field of the record and of its template; x toggles hexadecimal.
5 FlowLink › Log › IndicatorsIndicator L04State, id and name, Value, Origin, the explanation and the Next step.
5 FlowLink › Log › Events, 7 CaptureTextThe complete text of the event, command or path (useful when the line is cut).

The detail of a chain link is shown in "1 Home" and the one of a ready-made command in "7 Capture".

Pause, window and zoom in practice

How to freeze the screen to read it

  1. Press p. The header changes from ● LIVE to ■ FROZEN hh:mm:ss.
  2. Read, move and open details as usual; nothing changes under your eyes. Counters and captures keep running underneath.
  3. Press p again to follow. The next snapshot replaces the frozen one.

Expected result: the header shows the time of the freeze and the figures stop moving.

How to change the time window

  1. Press t to go through 1m → 5m → 15m → 1h (the header shows it). Or press + to zoom in and - to zoom out (- reaches ∞, "since fl-doctor opened").
  2. On the IPs tab t does not change the window: it copies the tshark command, so use + - there, or choose "Time window: …" in the palette.

Expected result: the Funnel title, the rankings and the evidence ladder follow the new window. It is never longer than the statistics window of the memory profile.

How to enlarge a panel

  1. Move the focus to the panel with Tab.
  2. Press z. The panel fills the whole body (useful on small terminals). Press z or Esc to go back.

Command palette, help and messages

  • Palette (: or Ctrl-P). Lists every action with fuzzy search (case- and accent-insensitive). Each action shows its shortcut and, when one exists, its command-line equivalent (for example fl-doctor evidence --ip IP --last 15m). It also lets you choose the window, capture engine, watch list and saved filters, show or hide columns, import watched IPs from a CSV, and reopen the tour (the "5-step tour" command).
  • Help (? or F1). Lists the keys for "This view" and the "Global" ones, with text filtering.
  • Messages (M). History of engine notices; ⏎ or y copy the selected one.

Command palette in detail

Press : (or Ctrl-P). A window opens with a text line (: …), the list of commands and, at the bottom, a hint line and the command-line equivalent of the highlighted command ("On the command line: …") or "(only exists in the interface)".

  • With an empty line it shows "Suggested and recent" commands.
  • Typing filters with a fuzzy search: the letters must appear in order, not together. A short, precise word works best (evid, memory, tutor); because the match is loose, an unrelated command can show up in the list, so read the title before ⏎.
  • The titles of the commands are always in English, also with the interface in Spanish.
  • Esc or Ctrl-P closes it. Ctrl-R switches to the history.

What the palette can do:

GroupCommands (titles as shown)
Go to"Go to Home (chain health)", "Go to Exporters", "Go to IPs (tracing)", "Go to Flows · ranking", "Go to Flows · live", "Go to IPs · seen (inventory)", "Go to FlowLink · service / configuration / log / batches", "Go to Host", "Go to Capture".
View"Toggle table and board", "Change the ranking grouping", "Change the sort order", "Freeze or follow the view", "Time window: 1m / 5m / 15m / 1h / ∞".
Filters"Type the global filter", "Clear the global filter", "Save the global filter with a name", and one command per saved filter ("Filter «name»: text").
IPs"Trace an IP", "Watch the selected IP", "Import watched IPs from a CSV", and one command per list ("Watch list: <name>").
Capture and evidence"Open the evidence wizard", "Dedicated capture to disk", "Capture the selected IP to disk (or stop the capture)", "Capture engine: auto / native / tcpdump / dumpcap".
Columns"Exporters: show / hide the <column> column", "Ranking: show / hide the <column> column".
Tool"Copy the selection", "Reread configuration, log and host", "Test the exit to the PCE", "Settings", "Settings · Memory & statistics", "Switch Spanish / English", "Next theme", "Shortcut help", "Message history", "5-step tour", "Quit".

How to find a command and see its command-line equivalent

  1. Press :.
  2. Type a few letters of the title (for example evid).
  3. Move with ↑ ↓; the last line shows the equivalent, such as fl-doctor evidence --ip IP --last 15m.
  4. Press ⏎ to run it or Esc to close.

Expected result: the command runs (for example it opens the evidence wizard) or the window closes. The equivalent is only a hint: it is not typed for you.

How to repeat something you did before

  1. Press Ctrl-R (from the screen) or : and then Ctrl-R. The title becomes "History (Ctrl-R)".
  2. Choose an entry. Each one carries its type at the right: command, filter, tool or copied.
  3. ⏎ runs the command again, applies the filter again or copies the saved command again. Tools only remember what you used (so that the most recent one is first in the capture form).
Note: The history shows each command with its palette title (for example "Settings") and you can search it by that title. Press Ctrl-R again to go back to the commands.

How to show or hide a table column

  1. Press : and type the start of the title, for example exporters: show the bytes.
  2. Run it with ⏎. The column is added at the end of the table (use Shift-→ to reach it if the terminal is narrow).
  3. To hide it again, search for "hide the …" with the same name. At least one column always stays.

The columns that can be added are, on 2 Exporters, bytes/s, IPs and Consumer; on 4 Flows › Ranking, Bytes, Packets, As source, As destination and /24 network. The choice is saved with the session state.

Help in detail

? (or F1) opens "Help · shortcuts": a Search: line, the keys for This view · <tab> first and then the Global ones. Type to filter by key or by description; the list scrolls with ↑ ↓ PgUp PgDn. If nothing matches, it says "No shortcut matches" and suggests erasing the text. The help of each tab is different: it lists the keys of the subview you are in.

Messages in detail

M opens "Messages": the notices that the engine sent (for example "Evidence package ready: …" or a capture that could not start). Interface hints such as "Copied" or "Bookmark saved" appear for a few seconds in a small box at the bottom right and are not kept. Each line shows a symbol, the time and the text; ⏎ or y copy the selected one, Esc or M close. When there is nothing, it says "There are no messages yet".

Language, theme and settings

  • L switches Spanish and English instantly and saves it. --lang es|en and FLDOCTOR_LANG set it for a single run.
  • T moves to the next theme: auto, brand (Illumio brand, truecolor), terminal (16 ANSI colors), light (light backgrounds) and mono (no color). NO_COLOR=1 also removes color.
  • , opens Settings with seven rows: Theme, Language, Color (auto, 16, 256, truecolor, no), Glyphs (unicode, blocks, ascii), Refresh (100, 250, 500, 1000, 2000 or 5000 ms), Bottom bar (full or minimal) and Mouse. Choose with ↑ ↓, change with ← →, Space or ⏎, and close with Esc or ,. Only what you change is saved.
  • S opens Settings › Memory & statistics (see "Memory and performance").

Settings, row by row

RowValuesWhat it changes
Themeauto, brand, terminal, light, monoPalette of colors. Same as T.
LanguageES, ENLanguage of explanations and notices. Same as L.
Colorauto, 16, 256, truecolor, noHow many colors fl-doctor uses; no is the same as NO_COLOR=1. Use truecolor if your terminal supports it but does not announce it.
Glyphsunicode, blocks, asciiSymbols: full Unicode (bars with eighth-of-a-block steps); blocks (the same symbols, but bars drawn with whole and half blocks, for fonts that lack the fine steps); or plain ASCII ([OK], [!!], [XX], # bars).
Refresh100, 250, 500, 1000, 2000, 5000 msHow often the screen is redrawn. A higher value uses less CPU.
Bottom barfull, minimalEvery hint of the panel, or a single one.
Mouseno, yesClick on a tab and wheel scrolling. Off by default (with the mouse captured you cannot select text by dragging).

How to change a setting

  1. Press ,. The window "Settings" opens with seven rows.
  2. Move with ↑ ↓ to the row and press → (or Space or ⏎) to go to the next value, ← for the previous one. The change applies at once.
  3. Press Esc (or ,) to close.

Expected result: the interface already uses the new value and config.toml holds only the preferences that you changed.

Themes

T goes through the themes without opening anything: auto (follows the terminal), brand (Illumio colors, truecolor), terminal (the 16 colors of your terminal), light (for light backgrounds) and mono (no color: states are told apart by symbol and word). The theme is saved. NO_COLOR=1 forces the mono look.

Language

L switches between Spanish and English at once, without restarting. Names of tabs, columns, keys and commands are always in English; descriptions, warnings, next steps and help follow the language. The ES/EN mark at the right of the tabs line shows the active one.

Go to, bookmarks and text boxes

Go to… (g)

Press g and then one letter. If you pause after g, a menu appears (after about 0.6 seconds) to remind you; any key that is not on the list cancels.

Bookmarks (m, ')

m followed by a letter saves where you are (tab, subview and selected row); ' followed by the letter takes you back. Lowercase bookmarks last for the session; uppercase ones are saved and survive when you close the tool. The notice "Bookmark saved: a" confirms it; if the letter does not exist it says so.

How to save a place and come back

  1. Go to the row you want to remember (for example an exporter on 2) and press m then a.
  2. Move around freely.
  3. Press ' then a. The tool returns to that tab and selects the same row.

Text boxes

Several actions ask you for a text in a small window: add an IP (+), trace an IP (r on 3 IPs), save a filter, import a CSV, and on 7 Capture the interfaces (i), ports (o) and BPF filter (b). They all work the same:

  • The first line explains what to type and gives an example; below it, the > line is where you type (paste works).
  • ⏎ accepts, Esc cancels. If the text is not valid, a red line says why and the box stays open so you can fix it.
  • The usual editing keys work (see "Inside windows and text fields").

Which side to watch

In Flows › Live every row has two IPs. Space asks "Which one to watch?" and you answer with one key: o source, d destination, a both, Esc cancel.

First use and the tour

The first time fl-doctor starts on an account, a three-step wizard asks about the symbols, the theme and the language, and then offers a five-step tour. Esc skips them; nothing is asked again.

StepQuestionKeys
1 of 3"Do these symbols look right in your terminal?" It draws ┌─┐ ▁▂▃▅▇█ ✓ ▲ ✗ ● ◆ ■ and its ASCII version.s, y or ⏎ yes; n use plain ASCII.
2 of 3"Pick the theme (←→ to see each one)": the real colors of OK, Warning, Failure, Info and the watched-IP mark.← → change, ⏎ next.
3 of 3"Pick the language (←→)".← → change, ⏎ finish.

The tour. Five pages: 1 "Home answers «what is wrong?»", 2 "Following an IP", 3 "Who sends what", 4 "Evidence for support", 5 "Palette, help and settings". Move with → / ⏎ and ←, close with Esc.

How to open the tour again

  1. Press : and type tutor (the command is called "5-step tour"; tour and 5-st find it too).
  2. Press ⏎.

Expected result: the window "Tour · step 1 of 5". The footer of the tour says "reopen with :tutor", and that is exactly what you type in the palette.

Filters

There are three places where you filter, depending on the tab:

WhereWhat it filtersHow
F on any tabGlobal: all viewsFilter menu with scope "all views".
/ on 4 Flows › RankingThe ranking only (its own filter; class private by default)Filter menu.
/ on 3 IPsThe IP list (Watched and Seen), for example ip 198.51.100.0/24Filter menu.
/ on 2 Exporters (table) and 5 FlowLinkOne-line text search (IP, name, version, consumer / log events)"Search:" bar. Esc clears it.

Filter menu

/ opens the menu with the view's scope and F with the global scope; g toggles between "this view" and "all views". The options are:

OptionWhat it does
IP or netIP, CIDR network or range, comma-separated.
Source / destinationThe IP or network on one side only (Tab toggles source and destination).
ExporterPick from the exporters seen.
PortPorts (6500, 2055…).
Protocoltcp, udp, icmp, sctp, gre…
Versionv5, v9, ipfix, sflow, text.
IP classprivate, public, cgnat, documentation, multicast, other.
Watch listWatch lists (list:<name>).
Type a filter…The full language, with live validation.

The lists show the values that were seen with their count (Space marks, ⏎ applies, Esc goes back). Fields validate as you type and show "N IPs match · M records in the window" or "A of B recent records match". Active filters appear as chips [ text ✕ ] (Tab moves focus to the chips, ← → choose one, ⏎ or Del remove it). At the end of the menu there are named saved filters and "+ Save current filter…". They are stored in filters.toml.

The menu step by step

The menu has three levels and you always come back to the first one:

  1. Options list. The title says the scope (Filter · Flows › Ranking · scope: this view (g)). At the top, the Active line shows the chips of the filter already applied; below it, a short explanation of what the filter means (for example class private = private IPs only (RFC 1918)).
  2. Values list (Exporter, Protocol, Version, IP class, Watch list). Each value shows how many records carry it. Space marks, ⏎ applies and returns to the options with the new chip; Esc returns without applying. If nothing is marked and you press ⏎, the filter of that type is removed.
  3. Text field (IP or net, Source / destination, Port, Type a filter…). It validates while you type: a green ✓ valid, the number of IPs and records that match, or a red message. ⏎ applies.

After a value list or a simple field (IP or net, Source / destination, Port) the menu stays open so that you can add more terms; "Type a filter…" and a saved filter apply and close the menu. Esc in the options list closes it. Terms of different types are joined with and; a new Port, Exporter, Protocol, Version or IP class term replaces the previous one of the same type, while IP and Source / destination terms accumulate.

Note: "Type a filter…" starts with the filter that is currently active. To start from scratch, press Ctrl-U first; to add to it, type and … after the existing text.

How to filter the ranking by one exporter

  1. Go to 4 Flows and press /. The title says "scope: this view".
  2. Move to "Exporter" and press ⏎. The list shows the exporters seen with their record count.
  3. Press Space on the one you want and ⏎.
  4. The menu comes back with the chip [ exporter 192.0.2.11 ✕ ]. Press Esc to see the ranking.

Expected result: the ranking only counts flows that came through that exporter, and the title of the panel carries the filter.

How to filter by a port

  1. Press /, choose "Port" and press ⏎.
  2. Type the number (for example 53) or several separated by commas, and press ⏎.

How to filter by protocol

  1. Press /, choose "Protocol" and press ⏎.
  2. Mark tcp, udp, icmp, sctp or gre with Space (the counts tell which ones occur) and press ⏎.

How to filter only one side (source or destination)

  1. Press /, choose "Source / destination" and press ⏎. The title says "(source)".
  2. Press Tab to switch to "(destination)".
  3. Type an IP, a CIDR network or a range and press ⏎.

How to save a filter and use it again

  1. With the filter you want, open the menu, press End to go to "+ Save current filter…" and press ⏎.
  2. In the text box, type a name (1 to 64 characters) and press ⏎. The notice "Filter saved: <name>" appears.
  3. Next time, open the menu: the filter is listed under Saved; ⏎ on it applies it. Del on a saved filter removes it. Saved filters are also in the palette ("Filter «name»: text").

Expected result: the saved filter survives the session (it lives in filters.toml).

How to remove filter terms

  1. Open the menu and press Tab: the focus goes to the chips on the Active line.
  2. Choose a chip with ← → and press ⏎ (or Del). Repeat for the next ones.
  3. Press Esc once to leave the chips and again to close the menu.

The global filter

F opens the same menu with the scope all views (g toggles the scope). A global filter limits Exporters, IPs, Flows and the funnel at once, and the header shows it as filter: …. Clear it from the palette ("Clear the global filter") or by removing its chips.

How to filter the whole tool by one exporter and one protocol

  1. Press F. The title says "scope: all views".
  2. Choose "Type a filter…" and type exporter 192.0.2.11 and proto udp. Press ⏎.
  3. Look at the header: filter: exporter 192.0.2.11 and proto udp.
  4. Visit the tabs; they all use that filter. To remove it, press :, type clear the global and press ⏎.

The text search bar

On 2 Exporters (table) and 5 FlowLink, / does not open the menu: it opens a one-line Search: bar at the bottom (Search: sw-core ✓ valid). It looks for the typed text in the exporter's IP, name, version or consumer, or in the log events. ⏎ applies it, ↑ ↓ bring back the earlier ones and Esc closes the bar. With the search applied, the title of the panel says search «sw-core» and Esc (outside the bar) clears it.

How to find an exporter by name

  1. Go to 2 Exporters and press /.
  2. Type part of the name or IP (sw-core) and press ⏎.
  3. Press Esc to see all of them again.

Filter language

The language is written in English. Spanish words from earlier versions (red, vigiladas, privadas, puertos…) still work and are rewritten to English automatically. It is case-insensitive.

KeywordValueWhat it filters
ipIP, CIDR network, range or list (198.51.100.20, 10.20.0.0/16, list:dns), comma-separatedIP on either side. A bare IP, network or list, without a keyword, counts as ip ….
net (network)CIDR networkSame as ip.
src (source), dst (destination)IP, network, range or listSource only / destination only.
exporterExporter IP or nameRecords from that exporter.
interfacecomma-separated namesCapture interfaces.
portsflowlink, all-udp, all or a list (2055,6500)Ports being captured.
portnumber(s)The record's source or destination port.
proto (protocol)icmp, igmp, tcp, udp, gre, esp, icmpv6, sctp or a numberIP protocol.
versionv5, v7, v9, netflow (v5, v7 and v9), ipfix, sflow, textExporter version.
transportudp, tcp, sctpTransport it arrived on.
consumernameFlowLink consumer.
vlan, ifin, ifoutnumber(s)VLAN and input / output interfaces (ifIndex).
bytesoperator and number: bytes > 1000, >=, <, <=, =Flow size.
dirin or outDirection.
classprivate, public, cgnat, documentation, multicast, otherIP class. private includes the documentation ranges.
private, public, cgnat—Shortcuts for class ….
watched—Watched IPs only.
expected / only expected—Only the site profile's expected networks.

How terms combine:

  • and (optional between terms), or, not and parentheses. Repeating a key adds values: ip A and ip B is the same as ip A,B (it looks for A or B).
  • or is only allowed between terms of the same key (version v9 or version sflow). Between different keys it is a clear error.
  • not is allowed before ip/src/dst/net, proto, class/private/public/cgnat, watched (equivalent to "not watched"), dir and bytes. Before any other key it is an error.
  • The text is limited to 4,096 characters. 
ip 198.51.100.0/24            exporter 192.0.2.11          interface ens192,ens224
ports 2055,6500               version ipfix                proto udp and port 53
not proto icmp                watched                      net 10.20.0.0/16
class private                 src 10.20.30.77              dst list:dns
bytes > 1000 and dir in       version v9 or version sflow  not class public
Note: The ranking on tab 4 starts with the class private filter ("private IPs only, RFC 1918"), which is removed like any other. In top (command line), --filter replaces that ranking filter.

Watching IPs

A watched IP is an IP, CIDR network or range that fl-doctor tracks exactly: it is counted precisely (not approximately), has its evidence ladder (N0–N4) and is always kept in the inventory of IPs seen.

How to watch

  1. Find the IP in any view (ranking, exporters, IPs seen, Live, Home's watched IPs).
  2. Press Space. The IP is marked with ◆ in every view and a notice appears: "watched in «list» (N)".
  3. To stop watching it, press Space again on the same IP (or Del in 3 IPs › Watched).

Special cases:

  • Flows › Live has two IPs per row. Space asks "Which one to watch?": o source, d destination, a both, Esc cancels. W watches the destination without asking.
  • Flows › Ranking grouped by /24 network watches the whole network. A watched network or range appears in the "Watched networks" table (Name, net, Records, IPs) in 3 IPs › Watched.
  • + on 3 IPs asks for "an IP, network or range and, if you want, a name": 198.51.100.20 dns-01. The name (1 to 64 characters) is optional.
  • If the IP is a member of a watched network, fl-doctor warns "It belongs to the watched network «…»" and does not delete the network.
  • When you watch an IP, a notice offers to capture its traffic to disk (C, with the cap in view). Nothing is stored until you accept.

Lists. Watched IPs are saved in the active list (the panel title says "Watched IPs · «list»") inside watchlist.toml. With the palette (:) you change the active list ("Watch list: …") and import IPs from a CSV (ip,name, with or without a header). The perfil list comes from site.toml and is not saved.

Limit of 1,024. Across all lists (watchlist.toml, the site profile and --ip) at most 1,024 IPs, networks or ranges are accepted. Anything beyond that is reported and does not enter the index or the watched and list: filters.

How to add an IP, a network or a range by typing it

You can type what to watch even if the IP has not appeared in any flow yet (it will show "No data yet" until it does).

  1. Go to 3 IPs (key 3). The Watched subview is the one that opens first; if you are in Seen, press [.
  2. Press +. A text box "Watch an IP, network or range" opens. Its first line shows the format: "IP, network or range and, if you want, a name: 198.51.100.20 dns-01".
  3. Type the target, a space and an optional name. Accepted targets:
TargetExample
One IP198.51.100.77 web-01
A CIDR network203.0.113.64/28 dmz-small
A range203.0.113.100-203.0.113.103 dns-range
  1. Press ⏎.

Expected result: the IP appears in the list with ◆ and the counter at the foot of the panel grows (for example 1/2). It also shows ◆ in every other tab. With a network or a range, the list gets one row per member that has been seen (all with the same name) and a table Watched networks appears below with Name, net, Records and IPs. Without a name, the name is the target itself; a name must have 1 to 64 characters.

If the text is not valid ("198.51.100" is not an IP), the box stays open with the red line "Type an IP, network or range, and an optional name"; fix it and press ⏎ again, or Esc to cancel.

Note: Adding with + stores the IP and nothing else: no packet is saved. Adding with Space also shows a notice that offers to capture its traffic to disk (C); that offer is only a notice, nothing is stored until you accept.

How to stop watching an IP

  1. In 3 IPs › Watched, choose the IP with ↑ ↓.
  2. Press Del. (In any other view, Space on the same IP does the same.)

Expected result: a notice "◇ 198.51.100.77 is no longer watched in «list»" and the row disappears. If the IP is only a member of a watched network or range, the notice says "It belongs to the watched network «name»" and nothing is removed: the table of watched networks is informational (its rows cannot be selected), so to remove a whole network or range delete its entry from watchlist.toml.

How to watch an IP from another view

  1. On any tab, put the selection on a row that carries an IP: an exporter on 2, a ranking row on 4, a row of Seen on 3 or a record in Live.
  2. Press Space (or w). The IP gets the ◆ mark in every view and the notice "◆ <ip> watched in «list» (N)" appears.
  3. Press Space again on the same IP to stop watching it.

On 4 Flows › Live a row has two IPs, so Space asks which one: o, d or a (see "Which side to watch"). On 4 Flows › Ranking grouped by /24 network, Space watches the entire network.

How to import many IPs from a CSV

  1. Prepare a text file with one ip,name per line (a header line is accepted).
  2. Press :, type import and press ⏎ ("Import watched IPs from a CSV").
  3. Type the path of the file and press ⏎.

Expected result: the IPs are added to the active list. If the file cannot be read, a red notice says so ("The watched-IP file could not be read (…)").

How to switch to another watch list

The palette has one command per list ("Watch list: <name>"); choose it and ⏎. The title of the panel shows the active list (Watched IPs · «name»). The list perfil comes from site.toml and cannot be edited from the tool.

Copy and quit

  • y copies the selection to the terminal clipboard (OSC 52); if the terminal does not support it (PuTTY, for example), Y saves it to a file. Whatever is copied or saved goes through the secrets redactor: if something was hidden, the interface tells you.
  • q or Ctrl-C quit. If there are disk captures running, it first asks what to do with them (see "Evidence for support › Dedicated capture and Keep running after exit").
  • On exit the tool saves the session state (last tab, window, columns, order, uppercase bookmarks).

What y copies in each place

WhereWhat y copies
2 Exporters, 3 IPs, 4 Flows › Ranking, 1 HomeThe IP of the selected row.
4 Flows › Livesource -> destination of the selected record.
5 FlowLink › Log (events panel)The text of the selected event.
7 Capture (commands panel)The selected command (it is also recorded in the history).
7 Capture (captures panel)The path of the selected capture.
Detail window, Messages, "Package ready"The text of the window / the message / the path of the package.

If a notice that offers something to copy is on screen, y copies that first. The notice "Copied (if the terminal does not get it, Y saves it to a file)." confirms it; if something that looked like a secret was hidden in the copy, another notice says so.

How to quit with disk captures running

  1. Press q (or Ctrl-C). If there are captures to disk, the window "Quit" says "There are N disk captures running." and lists up to three of them.
  2. Press s (or y, ⏎, Ctrl-C) to stop them and quit, or Esc (or n) to stay.
  3. Captures that you started with Keep running after exit are not stopped: the window says how many keep running and, after the terminal is restored, fl-doctor prints their pid and the command to stop them.

Without disk captures running, q quits at once. Ctrl-Z suspends the tool (come back with fg) and Ctrl-L redraws the screen if something else wrote over it.

Reference by tab

1 Home

What it shows. The A–E chain at a glance, the datagram funnel and the watched IPs. It answers "where does it break?".

The chain. Five links, each with a symbol, a word and a figure:

LinkWhat it coversChecks
A ExportersAre flows arriving from any switch or router, and well formed?A1 exporters seen · A2 version vs consumer · A3 templates · A4 template fields · A5 sampling · A6 loss on the path · A7 exporter clock · A8 fragmentation · A9 flow duration · A10 templates only
B HostInterface, kernel, firewall, rp_filter, clockB1 seen on the wire · B2 port without a listener · B3 socket discards · B4 rp_filter · B5 local firewall · B6 interface and duplicates
C FlowLinkService, configuration, ports, remote_addrsC1 service · C2 configuration · C3 ports · C4 remote_addrs
D DeliveryExit test to the PCED1 DNS · D2 proxy · D3 TLS · D4 available (node_available)
E PCEWhat happens inside the PCENot evaluated: it is outside the collector. It is documented in the evidence.

Each link shows its most serious check; if there are others in warning or failure, they appear below. ⏎ opens the detail: what was checked, where the datum came from and the next step.

How old the D checks are. The detail of D1–D4 ends with how long ago the exit test ran, for example · tested 12 s ago. The test repeats every 30 s while the interface is open (and again with P in 6 Host); if the last one is more than 120 s old, D1–D4 change to "no data" instead of showing as current a result that no longer is. With --offline the test never runs and D reads "not tested".

The funnel. Five rows that count what happens in the chosen window:

RowWhat it counts
wireDatagrams per second reaching the collector (the wire).
socketThose the kernel hands to a FlowLink socket. not measured if it could not be measured.
decodedRecords per second that are understood.
discardsRecords discarded per second, with the dominant protocol (for example ICMP 100 %).
deliveredBatches of the last cycle delivered with a 2xx response (for example 1/1 batches · 204, as in the screenshot below).

Below, a pps curve. The first step where the count drops sharply points to the link to check. With no datagrams, the panel says "No datagrams on UDP 6500 for N s" and what to look at (does the exporter point at the collector? the firewall? another port?).

Log indicators. On wide terminals (160 columns or more), a third panel lists the log indicators L01–L17 (see "5 FlowLink").

Watched IPs. A table with these columns:

ColumnWhat it shows
NameThe watched IP's name (◆).
IPThe address.
VerdictVerdict: "Delivered", "Waiting for the next cycle", "FlowLink does not receive it", "Received, not delivered", "Incomplete data", "Not seen, sampling active", "Not seen" or "No data yet".
LadderRungs reached: N1 N2 N3 N4 or ·· for the missing ones.
LastTime of the last record.
NoteFor example "next cycle in 3 min" or "does it pass through that device?".

How to see where the chain breaks

  1. Open sudo fl-doctor; tab 1 Home is the start tab.
  2. Look at the links from top to bottom. The first one with ▲ or ✗ is the one to check.
  3. Select that link (↑ ↓) and press ⏎.
  4. Read the detail: which check failed, where the datum comes from and the next step.

Expected result: a link with a symbol and a concrete sentence (for example "A5 · Sampling on: 198.51.100.12 1:10, 198.51.100.13 1:512…", as in the screenshot above) and a next step. Headless equivalent: sudo fl-doctor health.

Note: If fl-doctor does not run as root, Home shows a "Degraded mode" band at the top with what cannot be seen (capture, firewall, other users' processes) and where to look.

Panels and keys on Home

Home has up to four panels. Only two take the focus (Tab switches between them); the other two are indicators that follow along.

PanelTakes focusWhat you do there
Chainyes↑ ↓ choose a link (A to E); ⏎ opens its details; z enlarges it. A link shows its most serious check; below it, indented, the other checks that are in warning or failure.
Funnel · 15mnoFollows the time window of the header. Figures: wire, socket, decoded, discards, delivered, plus the pps curve.
Log indicatorsnoOnly at 160 columns or more. The indicators in order (L01, L02…) as many as fit in the height, each with its symbol; the complete list is in 5 FlowLink › Log.
Watched IPs · list «name»yes↑ ↓ choose an IP; ⏎ goes to 3 IPs with that IP selected; Space stops watching it; r, e, C act on it.

How to look at the details of a link

  1. On 1 Home, make sure the focus is on the Chain (its title has the ●; if not, press Tab).
  2. Choose the link with ↑ ↓. The ▶ marks it and the bottom bar shows where you are (Home › Chain › A Exporters).
  3. Press ⏎. The window "Link A · Exporters" opens with one block per check (A1, A2…): symbol, title, origin of the datum in brackets and, when needed, the Next step.
  4. Scroll with ↑ ↓ and close with Esc.

Expected result: you can tell which check of the link is in warning and what to do about it. For link E the window says that the PCE is outside the collector.

How to go from a watched IP on Home to its evidence ladder

  1. Press Tab to move the focus to the Watched IPs panel.
  2. Choose the IP and press ⏎.

Expected result: the tab 3 IPs opens with that IP selected and its ladder on the right.

2 Exporters

What it shows. One row for each exporter and destination port seen (a single switch sending to two ports appears twice). All received ports are shown, not only FlowLink's, precisely to catch the "exports to the wrong port" case.

Subviews. Table (default) and Board (d or [ ]).

Table columns. The first eleven are visible by default; the rest are added from the palette ("Exporters: show the … column").

ColumnWhat it shows
ExporterExporter IP and its name (from the site profile).
Ver.Export version: v5, v7, v9, IPFIX, sFlow or text.
PortDestination UDP port.
ppsDatagrams per second.
rec/sFlow records per second.
Tmpl.Templates received and whether they are complete (✓), missing fields (▲) or unchecked. — if it uses no templates.
SamplingAnnounced sampling (1:512). — if none.
LossLoss estimated from sequence gaps. Green under 1%, warning from 1%, failure from 5%.
ClockThe exporter clock's offset from the collector. Warning above 30 s.
FlowLinkWhether FlowLink accepts it (see below).
SeenHow long ago the last datagram arrived.
bytes/s (optional)Bytes per second.
IPs (optional)Distinct IPs, private / public.
Consumer (optional)The FlowLink consumer that applies to it.

The FlowLink column compares what arrives with FlowLink's configuration (each consumer's ports and remote_addrs):

TextMeans
✓ accepts (and · log)FlowLink accepts it; · log if it also appears in the log.
✗ no listenerIt arrives at a port where FlowLink is not listening (check B2/C3).
✗ not in remote_addrsThere is a consumer on that port, but the IP is not in its remote_addrs (C4).
▲ version ≠ parserThe version does not match the consumer's parser (A2).
▲ possibleIt cannot be confirmed that the parser handles that version.
· config not readThe config.yaml could not be read: it cannot be judged.

Detail panel. Beside or below the table: FlowLink (with the explanation and the associated check), Format (version and consumer), Templates (count, measured resend in seconds, complete or missing fields), Measures (sampling, loss, clock), Traffic (r/s, pps, bytes/s, private and public IPs), Other (fragmented, maximum duration) and Per minute (heat strip and curve). ⏎ widens it to the whole body.

Board (d). "Who sends the most · by records/s" ranks the exporters by volume: columns #, Exporter, Volume, Share (bar), %, Curve, IPs (private/public) and Consumer; on the right, a stacked curve per exporter. o changes the measure between records/s, bytes/s and datagrams/s.

Sort and search. In the table, o sorts by the next column (it starts at rec/s, descending) and O reverses the order. / opens the one-line text search; Esc clears it.

How to tell whether my switch is exporting and to which port

  1. Go to tab 2 (2).
  2. Find the switch's IP in the Exporter column. If there are many, use / and type part of the IP or name.
  3. Look at Ver. and Port. Compare them with the FlowLink consumer's port (tab 5 › Config).
  4. Look at the FlowLink column. If it says no listener or not in remote_addrs, open the detail with ⏎.

Expected result: a row with the version, the port and ✓ accepts. If the port is different, the detail says "Arrives at UDP 9995 but FlowLink listens on 2055, 4739, 6343 (B2/C3)", as in the screenshot below. Fixing the port on the switch, or adding a consumer in FlowLink, is up to you: fl-doctor changes nothing.

Tip: Missing templates explain undecoded v9/IPFIX records: the exporter resends them every so often. In the detail, "Templates" shows the measured resend. And with 1:N sampling, a low-traffic IP may not show up in a short window.

Table, panel and keys on Exporters

The tab has two subviews ([ ] or d): Table and Board. In the table, the left panel lists the exporters (one row per exporter and destination port) and the right panel, Details, always shows the selected one; the title of the right panel is <ip>:<port> · <name>. The foot of the left panel shows 1/4 (selected row / total). The title of the left panel is Exporters · N; with a search applied it adds search «text».

KeyWhat it does here

⏎Widens the Details panel to the whole body (⏎ or Esc go back).
/Search bar (IP, name, version, consumer).

How to see the details of an exporter

  1. Go to 2 Exporters (2).
  2. Choose the row with ↑ ↓. The right panel already shows the details: FlowLink, Format, Templates, Measures, Traffic, Other and Per minute.
  3. Press ⏎ to widen the panel to the whole body when the lines are cut; press ⏎ or Esc to go back.
  4. If the FlowLink line says ✗ no listener, read the explanation under it ("Arrives at UDP 2055 but FlowLink listens on 6343, 6500 (B2/C3)").

Expected result: every figure about that exporter in one place (version, template state and resend, sampling, loss, clock, rates, distinct IPs, fragmented datagrams, maximum duration) and, in the Per minute strip, its recent rate.

How to sort the table

  1. Press o: the table is sorted by rec/s (descending). Press o again for the next column (Tmpl., Sampling, Loss…).
  2. Press O to reverse the direction.

Expected result: a ▲ or ▼ next to the title of the sorted column, and the rows reordered. The order is kept with the session state.

How to show more columns or reach the ones that do not fit

  1. The first column (Exporter) stays; the others are hidden from the lowest priority when the panel is narrow. Press Shift-→ to slide the table: the columns on the left are hidden and the hidden ones on the right appear. Shift-← goes back. A ◀ +N mark on the foot of the panel says how many are out.
  2. To add the optional columns, press : and run "Exporters: show the bytes/s column", "…the IPs column" or "…the Consumer column" (see "Command palette in detail").

How to see who sends the most

  1. Press d (or ]). The title is "Who sends the most · by records/s".
  2. Press o to change the measure: records/s → bytes/s → datagrams/s.
  3. On the right, the stacked curve per exporter with its legend.

How to watch an exporter's address and copy it

  1. Choose the exporter and press Space: its IP becomes a watched IP (marked ◆). Press Space again to undo.
  2. Press y to copy the IP to the clipboard.

3 IPs

What it shows. Two subviews toggled with [ ]: Watched (the watched IPs and the tracing of the selected one) and Seen (the inventory of IPs seen).

Watched

On the left, the list of watched IPs (Name, IP and a verdict symbol) and, if there are watched networks or ranges, the "Watched networks" table. On the right, the Evidence ladder panel for the selected IP.

The evidence ladder. fl-doctor stops at the last verified rung and says where each datum comes from:

RungWhat it provesWhere the datum comes from
N0Not seen in the windowcapture (wire)
N1Reaches the collector inside the flowscapture (wire)
N2FlowLink has somewhere to receive it: listener, remote_addrs and a socket with no dropsconfiguration and kernel
N3FlowLink processed it (it appears in the log's new IPs or in reported_ips.dat)log
N4The cycle that included it was delivered (HTTP 204)log
EWhat happens in the PCEOutside the collector: it goes in the evidence for support

Below the ladder: the verdict, the Peers (other IPs, ports and protocols the IP talks to, with their percentage), the Exporters that report it, the Transport, a Per minute curve (records per minute), the Records and a sentence summarizing the ladder. If a cycle is in progress, it says "Waiting for the next cycle: it closes in N s".

With 1:N sampling on the exporter, the verdict "Not seen, sampling active" means a low-traffic IP may not show up, and fl-doctor calculates how long you would have to observe.

How to tell whether an IP shows up in the flows and how far it gets

  1. Go to tab 3. If the IP is already in the list, select it; if not, press +, type the IP (for example 10.20.30.77 app-nuevo-77) and ⏎. Alternatively, Space on the IP in any view.
  2. Let it run for a few minutes. To widen the window use - (on this tab + adds an IP and t does not change the window: it copies the tshark command).
  3. Read the ladder from top to bottom and stop at the first rung without ✓.

Expected result: the IP reaches a specific rung and the verdict translates it. Headless: sudo fl-doctor trace --ip 10.20.30.77 --observe 300.

What to do depending on where it stops:

  • N0: there is no traffic from that IP in the window. Before concluding anything, check the switch's sampling (tab 2), observe longer and confirm that the server's traffic really goes through the device that exports. If the exporter sits above the server segment, its IPs cannot appear no matter how long you observe.
  • N1 without N2: it arrives but FlowLink does not receive it. Check remote_addrs (it accepts single IPs, not CIDR) and the consumer's port. The lab probe in the screenshot below is this case.
  • N3 without N4: FlowLink processed it but the cycle was not delivered. Go to 5 FlowLink › Log.
  • N2 with a warning because "192.0.2.12 does not appear in FlowLink's log (L06)" (demo data): an exporter that reaches the wire is not in the log; check that switch.

Other actions on the list: r traces another IP you type (also a comma-separated list), e opens the IP's evidence, t copies its tshark command (it is recorded in the history), / filters the list (for example ip 198.51.100.0/24), Del removes the IP.

Reading the screen.

PartWhat it is
Panel title Watched IPs · «list»The active watch list. With a filter applied it adds the filter text (· ip 198.51.100.0/24).
Row ▌ ◆ dns-01 198.51.100.20 ▲▌ and ◆ mark a watched IP; then name, IP and the symbol of the verdict. The ▶ marks the selected row.
Foot of the panel 1/2Selected row over total rows.
Panel Watched networks · NNetworks and ranges: Name, net, exact Records and IPs seen. Informational: its rows cannot be selected.
Panel Evidence ladderThe ladder of the selected IP (N1 to N4 and E), the verdict, Peers, Exporters, Transport, Per minute and Records.
Last line of the ladderThe keys you can use: space watch · + add · / filter · e evidence · t tshark · c capture · r trace · Del remove.

How to trace an IP that is not in the list

  1. On 3 IPs press r. A text box "Trace an IP" opens ("One or more comma-separated IPs.").
  2. Type the IP (or several separated by commas), for example 203.0.113.5, and press ⏎.
  3. fl-doctor adds it to the list and selects it.

Expected result: the ladder of that IP. For an IP without traffic the first rung reads "N0 Not seen yet — no records for this IP in the window" and the verdict "No data yet"; wait a few minutes with the window open or widen it with -.

How to copy the tshark command for the selected IP

  1. Select the IP and press t.
  2. The notice "tshark command copied." appears. Paste it in another session of the collector.

Expected result: the clipboard holds the first ready-made tshark command of 7 Capture (the live one, tshark -ni <interface> -f '…'), written for the installed tshark version and the collector's ports. Until the first snapshot arrives, a notice says "There is no tshark command ready yet". The variant for a saved capture (tshark -2 -r …) is on 7 Capture and is copied from there with y.

How to filter the list of watched IPs

  1. Press /. The title says Filter · IPs · scope: this view (g).
  2. Choose "Type a filter…" and type ip 198.51.100.0/24; the box tells you how many IPs match.
  3. Press ⏎. The list shows only those; the title of the panel carries the filter.
  4. To remove it, press /, Tab and ⏎ on the chip, then Esc.

Seen

The inventory of IPs seen in the statistics window (30 minutes by default). You do not need to watch anything: it answers "of everything that arrives, which IPs does the collector see and which does FlowLink report?".

ColumnWhat it shows
IPThe address (◆ if watched).
First seen / Last seenFirst and last time within the window (UTC time).
RecordsNumber of records (≈ if the figure is approximate).
ExportersExporters it arrives through: the first four and +N.
FlowLink✓ reported if FlowLink reports it (according to reported_ips.dat), · not reported if not, or ? unknown.

On the right, the IPs seen panel summarizes: IPs seen, reported, not reported, "exact up to N IPs" (the profile's exact capacity) and, per exporter, how many IPs it brings and how many are reported. The top strip shows the current filter, sort and exporter (filter: all · sort: records · exporter: all).

How to see which IPs the collector saw and which FlowLink reports

  1. Go to tab 3 and press ] to switch to Seen.
  2. Press f to filter: reported (only those FlowLink reports), not reported (only those it does not) and all.
  3. Press o to sort (records, last seen, first seen, IP) and x to keep a single exporter.
  4. Press ⏎ on a row to see its details; Space watches it, C captures it to disk, e builds evidence and r traces it.

Expected result: the table shows only the IPs you asked for and the summary counts how many they are. An IP seen but not reported usually points to an earlier discard (for example remote_addrs, or a record FlowLink cannot interpret): watch it and follow the ladder.

Three details to avoid mistakes:

  • If reported_ips.dat could not be read, its format is not recognized or it was read incompletely, the column says ? unknown, not "not reported", and a notice explains it: without the complete file you cannot claim FlowLink does not report an IP.
  • The table has a fixed size (on the order of 100 thousand IPs in the normal profile; the exact figure appears in the panel as "exact up to"). If it overflows, the figures become ≈ and the summary says so. Watched IPs always get in; the ones with most records evict those with a single record. An IP that does not appear may still have been seen: to be sure, watch it.
  • "Reported" proves FlowLink processed the IP, not that the PCE received it. That is what ladder rung N4 is for.

Reading the Seen screen.

PartWhat it is
Strip under the subview namesfilter: all · sort: records · exporter: all: the filters in force. f, o and x change them.
Table title IPs seen · last 30 minThe statistics window of the profile (30 minutes by default), not the screen window t.
Row marks▶ selected row; ▌ ◆ watched IP.
First seen / Last seenTime (UTC) of the first and last record inside the window.
ExportersThe first exporters through which the IP arrived and +N for the rest.
FlowLink✓ reported, · not reported or ? unknown.
Right panel IPs seenTotals (seen, reported, not reported, "exact up to") and, under By exporter, how many IPs each exporter brings and how many are reported. The exporter in force is marked ▶.

How to see only the IPs that FlowLink does not report

  1. Go to 3 IPs and press ] to open Seen.
  2. Press f once for reported and twice for not reported; the strip says filter: not reported.
  3. Look at the right panel: the counts are those of the whole inventory; the table lists only the filtered rows.

Expected result: the table lists the IPs the collector saw and FlowLink did not report. Press f a third time to see all of them again.

How to see what a single exporter brings

  1. On Seen press x: the strip says exporter: 192.0.2.11 sw-core-01 and only the IPs seen through it remain. Press x again for the next exporter; after the last one it returns to all.
  2. In the right panel the By exporter list marks the one in force with ▶.

How to reorder the inventory

  1. Press o: records → last seen → first seen → IP → records…
  2. The strip shows sort: last seen (for example).

How to see the details of an IP seen

  1. Choose the row and press ⏎. The window "IP seen <ip>" opens.
  2. It shows First seen, Last seen (with how long ago), Records, the complete list of Exporters, the FlowLink status and whether it is Watched. At the bottom it lists the actions available from the row.
  3. Esc closes it; from the table you can then press Space, C, e or r on the same row.

How to look up one IP (or a network) in Seen and know whether FlowLink reports it

  1. On 3 IPs › Seen press /. The title says Filter · IPs · scope: this view (g).
  2. Choose "Type a filter…" (the ninth option: press ↓ eight times, or ⏎ on "IP or net" for a simpler box) and type ip 198.51.100.20 (a network such as ip 203.0.113.64/28 works too).
  3. Press ⏎. The table keeps only that IP (or the IPs of that network).
  4. Read the FlowLink column: ✓ reported, · not reported or ? unknown.
  5. To go back, press /, Tab, ⏎ on the chip and Esc.

Expected result: one row with the first and last time, the records, the exporters and the reported state. If the IP is not in the table at all, it was not seen in the statistics window (or it was evicted when the table overflowed): watch it with + or Space to track it exactly.

Note: The filter of Seen is the same one as the list of Watched; the strip filter: … · sort: … · exporter: … only shows f, o and x, not this filter. Open / to see it as a chip.

4 Flows

What it shows. Two subviews ([ ]): Ranking and Live.

Ranking

The top strip summarizes the parameters: group: IP · sort: flows · window 15m · filter: class private = private IPs only (RFC 1918).

ColumnWhat it shows
#Rank.
IPThe IP (or /24 network, or exporter, depending on the grouping). ◆ if watched.
NameName from the watch list or the profile.
FlowsNumber of flows; ≈ if approximate.
%Percentage of the total.
ShareProportional bar.
Arrives from (exporter)Main exporter and +N others.
PeersHow many distinct IPs it talks to.
SeenHow long ago it was seen.
Bytes, Packets, As source, As destination, /24 network (optional)Added from the palette ("Ranking: show the … column").

a changes the grouping (IP → /24 network → exporter) and o the sort order (flows, bytes, packets, peers, most recent). The panel on the right gives the breakdown by exporter of the selected row (Tab gives it focus, ⏎ opens it in a window): domain, input and output interfaces, flows and percentage, sampling and ×N estimate, and the source/destination split and main ports.

The ≈ symbol. Watched IPs, exporters, totals and log indicators are exact. The ranking of unwatched IPs uses an approximate counter (Space-Saving algorithm): the first rows are usually exact and carry no mark; the ones that may over-count carry ≈ and their error bound in the detail ("≈ approximate: it can over-count by up to N records; it never under-counts"). On the command line it appears as ~N (≤ +c) and the error_bound CSV column. The figure on a ≈ row is an upper bound: do not sort the tail of the ranking by flows without looking at the bound. For an IP's exact value, watch it with Space: from then on it is counted exactly. The ranking keeps at most 1,000 rows.

Board (d). Shows bars for the busiest IPs and, on the right, "Curves and breakdown": the curve of the total and of the first IPs, the split by IP class and by exporter.

Grouped by exporter (a twice) returns one row per exporter, with its flows and distinct IPs.

How to tell which IPs have the most flows and through which switch they arrive

  1. Go to tab 4 (4); it opens on Ranking.
  2. If something you do not care about dominates the ranking, press / and add a filter, for example not proto icmp or net 10.20.0.0/16.
  3. Press a to group by IP, /24 network or exporter, and o to change the sort criterion.
  4. Select a row and look at the breakdown on the right. For an exact value, press Space.

Expected result: a sorted list with the number of flows and the exporters each IP arrives through. Headless: sudo fl-doctor top --n 20 --observe 120 (or --by exporter).

Panels and keys on Ranking. The left panel is the ranking (IPs with the most flows · N records · M IPs (K private)); the right panel is the breakdown of the selected row (<ip> · by exporter). Tab switches the focus between them.

KeyWhat it does
↑ ↓, PgUp PgDn, Home EndMove the selection; the breakdown follows.
⏎Opens the breakdown in a window (title <ip> · breakdown).
aGroup: IP → /24 network → exporter.

/Filter menu of the ranking (its own filter, class private by default).
