How to see through which exporters an IP arrives

  1. Choose the IP in the ranking. The right panel lists, for each exporter, the observation domain, the input and output interfaces (if 2→10), the number of flows with percentage and bar, and — when the exporter samples — sampling 1:512 estimate ×N ≈12,288 (the sampled count multiplied by the rate). The last line gives the source / destination split and the main ports.
  2. For more room, press Tab and then ⏎: the same text opens in the window <ip> · breakdown, with Flows, Peers, Bytes, Packets and Seen above.

How to add or hide columns, and reach the ones that do not fit

  1. Press : and run "Ranking: show the Bytes column" (and "…Packets", "…As source", "…As destination", "…/24 network"). The column is added to the right.
  2. Press Shift-→ to slide the table until you reach it (the first column # stays in place).
  3. To hide it again run "Ranking: hide the … column".

How to change the grouping and the sort order

  1. Press a: the strip changes to group: /24 network, and with a second a, group: exporter; a third a goes back to IP.
  2. Press o: sort: bytes, then packets, peers, most recent and back to flows.

Expected result: the strip under the subview names always spells out the group, the sort, the window and the filter in force.

Live

Records as they arrive, with source and destination together. They are kept only while the view is open and in a fixed-size ring (500 rows in lean, 2,000 in normal and large). If memory reaches the critical level, Live closes and says so.

ColumnWhat it shows
TimeRecord time.
Source → DestinationThe flow's two IPs.
ProtoProtocol (udp, tcp, icmp…).
Bytes, PktsFlow size.
Exporter, Ver.Exporter and version.

p pauses so you can read; ⏎ opens the record with all its template fields (Time, Exporter, Source, Destination, Protocol, Bytes / packets, ICMP type/code, Interfaces (ifIndex), Sampling, Next hop, Capture interface, Template, Template fields) and x shows it in hexadecimal; Space asks which side to watch and / opens the filter menu.

Reading the screen. The title is Live · N recent records (Live (frozen) · N records when paused). The Source → destination column shows ip:port → ip:port; the if column shows the input and output interface indexes (4→10); Ver. is the exporter's flow version (v9, IPFIX, sFlow). The newest record is first and the list is cut at the ring size.

How to pause and read a record in full

  1. Press p: the header changes to ■ FROZEN and the list stops.
  2. Choose a row and press ⏎. The window "Flow record" lists every field: Time, Exporter (address, port, version and observation domain), Source, Destination, Protocol (name and number), Bytes / packets, Interfaces (ifIndex), Sampling, Capture interface and — when the record has them — ICMP type/code, Next hop, Template and Template fields.
  3. Press x to show the raw value of each template field in hexadecimal (it changes only records that carry template fields). y copies the text. Esc closes.
  4. Press p again to follow.

Expected result: every piece of the record readable at once, with nothing moving.

How to watch the source, the destination or both

  1. Choose the row in Live and press Space. The question "Which one to watch?" lists the two IPs.
  2. Press o for the source, d for the destination or a for both (Esc cancels).
  3. To watch the destination without being asked, press W.

Expected result: the notice "◆ <ip> watched in «list» (N)" and the ◆ mark on every row with that IP.

How to filter Live

Press /. The menu is the same as in the Ranking (IP or net, Source / destination, Exporter, Port, Protocol, Version, IP class, Watch list, Type a filter…). Live has no filter of its own: what you choose here is the global filter (the same one F edits), so it also affects the other tabs. While you type, a preview line says "A of B recent records match".

5 FlowLink

What it shows. FlowLink's state as seen from the collector, in four subviews ([ ]): Service, Config, Log and Batches. R rereads configuration, log and host.

Service

Four cards:

CardFields
ProcessStatus (with the pid), Executable, Unit, User, Start (and how long ago), Unit restarts, Command (with secrets hidden).
VersionVersion, Mode (systemd service or legacy), Log (path and whether it can be read).
Destination (PCE)pce_addr, org_id, api_key (only "present and readable" and its permissions; never the value), https_proxy/http_proxy.
Own consumptionfl-doctor's CPU and memory.

If it cannot find the process, it says why and what to look at (systemctl status illumio-flowlink, journalctl -u illumio-flowlink).

Config

FlowLink's config.yaml validated key by key, with secrets hidden:

  • Configuration file: path, whether it is readable and whether it is valid.
  • Parameters: pce_addr, org_id, api_key, data_directory, aggregation_minutes, data_directory_size_mb, file_retention_hours, metrics_print_seconds and proxy_config. Each with ✓, ▲ or ✗ and, if it fails, the reason (for example Additional property port is not allowed).
  • One card per consumer with parser.type, connectors, ports and remote_addrs (empty = accepts any exporter). remote_addrs with a mask are flagged "is not an IP (no masks)".
  • Validation errors and warnings, if there are any.

Log

Three blocks:

  1. Cycles, meters and discards. The timeline of aggregation cycles (every aggregation_minutes, 10 by default; ██ closed cycle, ░░ in progress) with batches, responses (204×48) and flush. Below, each consumer's rate (meter: 1 min and 15 min, with ▲ consumer without data if a consumer receives nothing) and the bad data discards with the dominant protocol (ICMP 100.0 % (echo …, unreachable …)). If it discards flows that are not ICMP, it warns ("discards N flows that are not ICMP").
  2. Indicators L01–L17 (left panel, symbol + name + value).
  3. Log events (right panel): time, symbol and event. Events: start (with the version), stop, send errors (with the cause: DNS, timeout, connection refused, TLS, proxy or other), cycles with flows, batches and 2xx responses, and cycles with no flows.
IndicatorWhat it measures
L01 Log aliveThe log is being written.
L02 Starts and configurationStarts and version.
L03 ConsumersWhat the last start announced against the open sockets.
L04 Rate per consumerRate per consumer (meter).
L05 Counter resetCounter resets.
L06 Exporters seen by FlowLinkThe wire's exporters against the log's.
L07 Data without templateData that arrived without a template.
L08 Aggregation cycleCycle frequency.
L09 Cycle deliveryBatches delivered in the cycle.
L10 Last batch deliveredHow long ago the last batch went out.
L11 Send errorsSend errors (Error sending request, DNS, i/o timeout).
L12 PCE response codesPCE response codes (204×N).
L13 "bad data" discards"bad data" discards and their protocol.
L14 New IPs per cycleNew IPs per cycle.
L15 Pending batchesBatches not yet delivered.
L16 General errorsGeneral log errors.
L17 Log sizeLog size.

Tab switches between indicators and events, ⏎ opens the detail with the next step and / searches the events. With the interface in Spanish, the indicator names are shown translated.

Batches

The pending batches (traffic_flows_*) that FlowLink has not yet managed to deliver to the PCE: count, size, the oldest, retention and data directory use against its limit (data_directory_size_mb). If the PCE cannot accept the batches, FlowLink stores them on disk and retries later; the count and age say since when nothing has been delivered. Warning from 90% of the limit; failure if the oldest exceeds retention.

How to check that the configuration and the sends to the PCE are right

  1. Go to tab 5 and press ] until Config. Check that Valid shows ✓ and that each consumer is green.
  2. Press ] until Log. Look at the cycle line: every closed cycle should have 204 responses.
  3. Check L11, L12, L13 and L15. If there are send errors, open the detail with ⏎.
  4. If there is no 204 at all and the log shows DNS or connection errors, go to 6 Host and press P to test the exit to the PCE.

Expected result: closed cycles with all their batches answered 204 (1/1 batches · 204 in the lab screenshot above), L11 at zero or with only old errors, and few pending batches. Headless: sudo fl-doctor log --since 2h.

Moving around inside 5 FlowLink

The four subviews have a strip of names under the tabs ([Service] Configuration Log Batches) where the current one is in brackets. Three ways to change:

  • [ and ] go to the previous / next subview (they wrap around).
  • g then a letter jumps directly: g l Log, g c Configuration, g w Batches. The 5 key opens the subview where you were last (Service the first time).
  • The palette: "Go to FlowLink · service / configuration / log / batches".

Service, Configuration and Batches are scrollable documents: ↑ ↓ PgUp PgDn scroll them and the foot of the panel shows which lines you see (1-18/25). On a wide terminal the cards sit side by side and everything fits; on a small one they stack and you scroll. R rereads the configuration, the log and the host (notice "Rereading configuration, log and host…").

Log, step by step

How to read the cycles line

  1. Go to 5 FlowLink and press ] twice (or g l). The top block is Cycles, meters and discards.
  2. The first line shows the cycles of the last hours (13:32 ██ 13:42 ██ … 14:22 ░░ (in progress)), the number of batches, the responses (204×48) and the flush time.
  3. The meter lines give each consumer's rate over 1 and 15 minutes; ▲ consumer without data marks a consumer that receives nothing.
  4. The bad data discards line gives the rate and the dominant protocol.

Expected result: you can tell at a glance whether FlowLink closes its cycles, sends them and gets 2xx answers.

How to see the explanation of an indicator

  1. Make sure the Indicators L01–L17 panel has the focus (its title carries the ●; Tab switches between indicators and events).
  2. Choose the indicator with ↑ ↓ (for example L04) and press ⏎.
  3. The window "Indicator L04" shows the state word (OK, Warning, Failure, No data, Info), the Value, the Origin (wire, kernel, config, log, inferred), the explanation and the Next step.

How to read a log event in full

  1. Press Tab to give the focus to Log events (the bottom bar says FlowLink › Log › Log events).
  2. Choose an event and press ⏎: the window "Text" shows it complete. y copies it.

How to search the events

  1. With the focus on the events press / and type a word (for example cycle).
  2. Press ⏎. The title becomes Log events · search «cycle» and only matching events remain.
  3. Esc clears the search.

Batches in practice

The Batches card says how many traffic_flows_* files are waiting, their size, how old the oldest one is, the retention and the use of the data directory against data_directory_size_mb (31.0 MB / 500.0 MB (6.2%)). A few pending batches can be normal while a cycle is being sent; a growing number, or an "oldest" that keeps getting older, suggests that the PCE is not accepting the sends: look at the Log (L11, L12) and at 6 Host (exit to the PCE).

6 Host

What it shows. A scrollable document (↑ ↓ PgUp PgDn) with cards about the host, all read-only. They are laid out in one, two or three columns depending on the width.

CardWhat it shows
HostName, operating system, kernel and whether it runs as root (without root, "not root: degraded mode").
Resourcesfl-doctor's memory, the host's, pressure and discards (see "Memory and performance").
InterfacesFor each interface: up or down, packets per second, recent drops, IPs, VLAN and master.
Kernel UDP countersInDatagrams, NoPorts, RcvbufErrors, InErrors (and InCsumErrors, SndbufErrors if not zero), with what accumulated since you opened fl-doctor and the last interval.
UDP socketsUDP sockets with their port (◆ for FlowLink's), receive queue, drops and the owning process. It warns if a FlowLink port has no socket.
rp_filter and return routerp_filter per interface (0 off, 1 strict, 2 loose) and the return route to each exporter, with an asymmetric-route warning.
Firewall (read-only)Engine (firewalld, nftables, iptables), whether it is active and, for each FlowLink port, whether it is allowed or blocked.
ClockWhether it is synchronized, offset and source.
Exit to the PCE (D1–D4)DNS, proxy (CONNECT), TLS (with the certificate issuer) and node_available, each with HTTP status and milliseconds, and how long ago it was tested.
What cannot be seenWhat could not be read (no root, missing command) and how to fix it.

Two notes on these cards:

  • NoPorts means datagrams arrive at a port with no socket (check B2); RcvbufErrors, that the socket buffer filled up (B3). With rp_filter = 1 (strict), the kernel may drop packets if the return route is asymmetric (B4).
  • The PCE exit test carries no credentials and is not run with --offline. P repeats it.

How to check the collector's exit to the PCE

  1. Go to tab 6 (6).
  2. Press P to repeat the test (it shows "Testing the exit to the PCE…").
  3. Look at the Exit to the PCE (D1–D4) card.

Expected result: D1, D2 (if there is a proxy), D3 and D4 with ✓ and their timings. A failure at D1 points to DNS; at D2, to the proxy; at D3, to TLS (the certificate issuer is shown, useful if there is TLS inspection).

Reading Host line by line

LineHow to read it
✓ ens192 up — drops +0 192.0.2.200 (Interfaces)Symbol, interface name, up or down, packets per second (— when it is not measured), packets dropped by the interface since the last reading (drops +N), its IPs, vlan N and the master interface if it has one.
◆ 6500 0.0.0.0 queue 0 B ✓ drops 0 … (UDP sockets)◆ marks a port FlowLink listens on; then the local address, the receive queue in bytes, the drops of that socket and the owning process. A FlowLink port without a socket is reported as "UDP 6500: no socket is listening (is FlowLink running?)".
✓ NoPorts 96 opening +0 · last — (Kernel UDP counters)The absolute counter of the kernel, what it added since you opened fl-doctor (opening +N) and in the last interval (last). What matters is the increase, not the absolute value.
✓ all 0 · off (rp_filter)The rp_filter value of all, default and each interface (0 off, 1 strict, 2 loose) and, below, the return route to each exporter (192.0.2.11 → ens192 and arrives on ens192; a mismatch is flagged "asymmetric route").
Engine firewalld · active (Firewall)The firewall engine found, whether it is active, and each FlowLink port as ✓ allowed or ✗ blocked; with firewalld it also lists the zone and its open ports. Read-only.
Synchronized ✓ (Clock)Whether the host clock is synchronized, the offset and the source (for example chrony). The exporters' offsets (A7) are measured against it.
✓ D1 DNS … · 18 ms (Exit to the PCE)One line per test with its result, HTTP code and time. D3 adds Certificate issuer: …. The last line says how long ago the test ran and that P repeats it.
1-19/50 at the foot of the panelWhich lines of the document you are looking at, out of the total.

The layout depends on the width. On a wide terminal Host is a three-column mosaic that fits without scrolling; on a small one it is a single column that you scroll with ↑ ↓ PgUp PgDn (Home and End go to the ends).

How to find out why datagrams get lost on the collector

  1. Go to 6 Host. Look at Kernel UDP counters: if NoPorts increases, datagrams arrive at a port where nobody listens (check B2); if RcvbufErrors or InErrors increase, the socket buffer overflowed (B3).
  2. In UDP sockets, look for the FlowLink ports (◆): a growing queue or drops on a socket confirms it.
  3. In rp_filter and return route, a value 1 with an asymmetric route explains packets dropped by the kernel before they reach FlowLink (B4).
  4. In Firewall, check that each FlowLink port says ✓ allowed.

Expected result: you can tell whether the loss happens in the network (it never reaches the wire), in the kernel (counters) or in FlowLink's socket (queue and drops).

7 Capture

What it shows. The capture engine, ready-made commands to use in another session, the disk captures in progress and the last evidence package.

PanelContent
Capture engineStatus (capturing / no capture), engine and interface, generated BPF filter, packets seen / lost / duplicated / reassembled and the available engines (missing ones, with the command to install them).
Ready-made commandstcpdump, dumpcap and tshark commands already built with the collector's ports and the watched IPs; the tshark one adapts to the installed version. The most recently used tool comes first.
Captures to disk in progressColumns #, Tool, File, Size (bar against the cap), Losses and Time (elapsed / limit).
EvidenceThe last package: path, SHA-256, size and notices.

Keys.

KeyAction
uChanges the engine: auto → native → tcpdump → dumpcap.
iChooses the capture interfaces (comma-separated; empty = all that have an IP).
oChooses the ports: flowlink, a list (2055,6500), all-udp or all.
bTypes a BPF filter by hand (empty goes back to the generated one).
cOpens the dedicated disk capture (form).
s or DelStops the selected capture (with focus on "Captures to disk"; Tab switches panel).
yCopies the selected command or the capture's path.
eOpens the evidence wizard.

Changing the interface or the ports reconfigures the capture on the fly. The BPF filter cannot filter by the IPs inside the records (their position depends on the template): that is why the tshark command comes afterwards.

How to get the ready-made capture commands

  1. Go to tab 7 (7).
  2. With ↑ ↓ choose the command (tcpdump, dumpcap or tshark).
  3. Press y to copy it and paste it in another session on the collector.

Expected result: the command is on the clipboard (or, with Y, in a file). Headless: fl-doctor commands --ip 198.51.100.20.

Panels and focus on Capture

The tab has four panels: Capture engine (top left), Ready-made commands (below it), Captures to disk in progress (top right) and Evidence (bottom right). Tab moves the focus between the commands and the captures to disk; the other two are informative. The foot of the focused panel shows 1/4 (selected / total).

Each ready-made command takes three lines: a header with the tool, a short description ("tcpdump to disk, 10 × 100 MB ring — used 5 s ago") and the command itself; the third line is a note (for example the limit of the BPF filter, or the syntax of the installed tshark). The tool used most recently comes first. ⏎ opens the complete line in a window ("Text"); y copies it.

How to copy a command and see it complete

  1. Go to 7 Capture. The focus is on Ready-made commands; if not, press Tab.
  2. Choose the command with ↑ ↓. Press ⏎ to read it complete and Esc to close.
  3. Press y. The notice "Copied (if the terminal does not get it, Y saves it to a file)." appears.

Expected result: the command in the clipboard, ready to paste in another session of the collector. Pasting it needs root to capture.

Changing what is captured

How to change the capture engine

  1. Press u. The engine goes auto → native → tcpdump → dumpcap → auto (the choice is saved).
  2. Read the Capture engine panel: Status, Engine and interface, the BPF filter, the Packets seen / lost / duplicated / reassembled and Available, which lists the engines found (✓ tcpdump 4.99.1, ✓ native) and the ones missing, with the command to install them (✗ dumpcap (install: dnf install wireshark-cli)).

auto picks the best engine available on the host; the header (capture ✓ native ens192) always shows the one in use. The built-in native engine needs no external tool.

How to choose the interfaces, the ports or a BPF filter

  1. Press i, o or b. A text box opens with its own help line.
KeyText boxWhat to type
i"Capture interfaces"Names separated by commas (ens192,ens224). Empty = all that have an IP.
o"Capture ports"flowlink (the ports of FlowLink's consumers), a list (2055,6500), all-udp or all.
b"Hand-written BPF filter"A BPF expression (udp port 6500). Empty goes back to the filter generated for the FlowLink ports.
  1. Press ⏎. The capture is reconfigured on the fly and the panel shows the new filter.
  2. Esc cancels. An invalid port list is rejected with a red line when you press ⏎.

The dedicated capture form

c opens "Dedicated capture to disk", a form with seven fields. It starts a tcpdump or dumpcap writing to disk in a ring of files, with a time limit and a size limit.

FieldValues and keys
Tool← → switch between tcpdump and dumpcap (the one that is installed and the most used comes first).
InterfacesText, comma-separated; empty = all.
BPF filterText; empty = "(the one generated for the FlowLink ports)".
Maximum duration← → change it by steps, or type digits; limited to 240 minutes (1,440 with Keep running after exit).
Ring files← → ±1 (up to 1,000).
MB per file← → ±10 (up to 10,000).
Keep running after exitSpace, ← or → toggle [ ] / [x]; off by default.

Below the fields the form always shows the summary ("Ring of 11 × 110 MB, limit of 15 min.") and the rule "Every capture to disk has a duration limit and a size limit." With Keep running after exit on, it adds the warning in yellow: "It keeps capturing as root after fl-doctor closes, 24 h at most. On exit you get its pid, the time left and the command to stop it."

How to start a capture to disk for 15 minutes

  1. Press c. The form opens on the field Tool.
  2. Move with Tab or ↓ to Maximum duration and set 15 with → or by typing.
  3. Adjust Ring files and MB per file if you need a different total size (the summary line multiplies them).
  4. Press ⏎ to start. fl-doctor goes to 7 Capture and the notice "Capture started: the path appears in the Capture tab." appears.
  5. Press Tab to move to Captures to disk in progress: the row shows the tool, the file, the size against the cap, the losses and the elapsed time.
  6. To stop it, choose the row and press s or Del.

Expected result: a row with a growing size and a rec ● mark in the header. A new tcpdump file appears in /var/tmp/fl-doctor/capturas/<private folder>/. (In fl-doctor demo the capture cannot start because the output folder does not exist; the form screens below are from the demo, and the next one is from the lab collector with a capture running.)

Use cases

Each case starts from a question, gives the steps in the interface (and the headless equivalent), and says what to expect and what to do next. The screens for each step are in "Reference by tab".

UC1 — Is everything OK? (Home)

The question: "Where does the chain break?"

  1. Open sudo fl-doctor and stay on tab 1 Home.
  2. Go through links A–E: the first one with ▲ or ✗ is the one to check. Look at the funnel too: the first step where the count drops sharply points to the link.
  3. Select the link in warning or failure and press ⏎.

Expected result: a detail with the check, the datum behind it and the next step. Headless: sudo fl-doctor health.

Next: follow the next step. For example, an A link in warning leads to 2 Exporters; a B link, to 6 Host; a C link, to 5 FlowLink › Config; a D link, to 5 FlowLink › Log and the PCE exit test. See "Reference by tab › 1 Home".

UC2 — Which switches are sending flows? (Exporters)

The question: "Is my switch exporting to the collector, in which format, and to which port?"

  1. Go to 2 Exporters.
  2. Find the switch in the table and compare Ver. and Port with what you expect.
  3. Look at the FlowLink column. If it says no listener or not in remote_addrs, open the detail with ⏎.
  4. Press d to see the "who sends the most" board.

Expected result: one row per exporter with version, port, templates and sampling. If a switch shows up sending NetFlow v5 to port 9995 while FlowLink listens on 2055, 4739 and 6343 (the case of sw-lab-04 in the lab), the row is flagged no listener and the detail says which ports FlowLink does listen on.

Next: fix the destination port on the switch or add a consumer in FlowLink (fl-doctor changes nothing). Watch for missing templates (v9/IPFIX cannot be decoded until the template arrives) and sampling. See "Reference by tab › 2 Exporters".

UC3 — Does this IP show up in the flows? (IPs › Watched)

The question: "Do I see flows from server 10.20.30.77, and how far do they get?"

  1. Go to 3 IPs › Watched. Add the IP with + (or Space on it in any view).
  2. Select the IP and read the evidence ladder.
  3. If it stops before N4, follow the rule in "Reference by tab › 3 IPs › Watched".

Expected result: a verdict ("Delivered", "Waiting for the next cycle", "FlowLink does not receive it"…) and the N1–N4 ladder with the source of each datum. Headless: sudo fl-doctor trace --ip 10.20.30.77 --observe 300.

Next: at N0, check the exporter's sampling and capture point; at N1 without N2, remote_addrs and port; at N3 without N4, 5 FlowLink › Log. fl-doctor never says "it reached the PCE": rung E is left for review with the evidence package.

UC4 — Which IPs have the most flows and through which switch do they arrive? (Flows › Ranking)

The question: "What generates the most traffic on the collector? Which switch reports it?"

  1. Go to 4 Flows (Ranking).
  2. If something you do not care about dominates the ranking, filter with / (for example not proto icmp).
  3. Change the grouping with a and the sort with o; open the row's breakdown with ⏎.

Expected result: each row carries its number of flows and the exporters it arrives through. Headless: sudo fl-doctor top --n 20 --observe 120 or --by exporter.

Next: watch with Space the IPs you care about to get their exact count and ladder. Remember that ≈ is an upper bound. Flows › Live shows the records one by one. See "Reference by tab › 4 Flows".

UC5 — Which IPs did the collector see and which does FlowLink report? (IPs › Seen)

The question: "Of everything that arrives, which IPs does FlowLink report to the PCE and which not?"

  1. Go to 3 IPs and press ] to open Seen.
  2. Press f to see only the reported or only the not reported; x for one exporter; o to sort.
  3. Watch (Space) the not-reported IPs you care about and follow their ladder.

Expected result: the filtered table and a summary with IPs seen, reported and not reported, and IPs per exporter.

Next: if you see ? unknown, there is no way to claim it is not reported (reported_ips.dat is missing or incomplete). "Reported" proves FlowLink processed it, not that the PCE received it. See "Reference by tab › 3 IPs › Seen".

UC6 — Are the configuration and the sends to the PCE right? (FlowLink › Config and Log)

The question: "Is FlowLink configured correctly and does it upload the batches to the PCE?"

  1. Go to 5 FlowLink › Config and confirm everything is valid.
  2. Switch to Log with ] and look at the cycles and responses.
  3. If there is no 204 at all, go to 6 Host and test the exit to the PCE with P.

Expected result: a valid configuration and cycles with all their batches answered 204 (1/1 batches per cycle in the lab). An L11 with old DNS errors that already recovered is not a problem if the cycles after them are delivered. Headless: sudo fl-doctor log --since 2h.

Next:

  • No 204 and DNS or connection errors: the problem is between the collector and the PCE (name resolution, firewall, proxy). In a field project, that was the reason FlowLink never uploaded anything.
  • Lots of "bad data": look at the protocol fl-doctor reports. In a telco project those discards were 100% ICMP (a field observation, not a rule documented by Illumio). If the dominant protocol is another one, treat it as a data problem.
  • Config in red: fix the indicated key and restart FlowLink yourself: fl-doctor does not do it.

UC7 — Evidence for support

The question: "What do I send to support?"

  1. Select the IP of interest (or leave it watched) and press e on any tab.
  2. Go through the four wizard steps (see "Evidence for support").
  3. Copy the package off the collector with the command fl-doctor prints.

Expected result: a .tgz with its SHA-256 in /var/tmp/fl-doctor/ and the exact command to copy it. Headless: sudo fl-doctor evidence --ip 10.20.30.77 --last 15m --pcap both.

Next: review the content with fl-doctor read <package>.tgz before sending it. There are no automatic copies.

UC8 — Memory and its indicator

The question: "How much memory does fl-doctor use? Can it bother FlowLink?"

  1. Look at the header: mem ● 23/64 MB · system 3.0 GB free: what fl-doctor uses against its budget and the host's free memory.
  2. Open 6 Host › Resources for the detail (peak, components, cgroup, pressure, discards).
  3. Press S to change the profile, window, black box or sampling.

Expected result: usage stays on a plateau below the budget, with ●. See "Memory and performance".

Next: if the symbol turns to ▲ or ✗, fl-doctor has already shrunk itself; if the collector is tight on memory, use --memory lean.

Evidence for support

Wizard (steps 1–4)

e opens the wizard from any tab, with the selected IP (or the watched ones) already loaded. It can always be cancelled with Esc. Keys: Tab/↑ ↓ change field, ← → change the value, Space marks, PgDn or ⏎ advance, PgUp goes back.

StepWhat you choose
1 of 4 · WhatIPs: IP, CIDR network, range or list:name, comma-separated (up to 64). Window: since fl-doctor opened, last N minutes (up to 1,440) or a new capture of N minutes (up to 60). Minutes: ← → add or subtract 5, or type the number. Exporters: checkboxes; none marked = all.
2 of 4 · Contentsevidence pcap: no pcap / original / trimmed / original and trimmed. decoded records per IP: no records / CSV / JSON / CSV and JSON. FlowLink log excerpts, configuration without secrets, host state, exit to the PCE (DNS, proxy, TLS): checkboxes. It shows the estimated size (≈) and warns if it exceeds 200 MB.
3 of 4 · Privacy"Pseudonymize in CSV/JSON the IPs that are not of interest". The original pcap is not touched: if it carries third-party data, you are warned.
4 of 4 · ConfirmSummary and chain status, output path, estimated size and the equivalent command (fl-doctor evidence --ip … --last …). ⏎ builds the package.

By default the contents are: original pcap, records in CSV, log excerpts, configuration without secrets, host state and PCE exit. If you choose "a new capture of N minutes", fl-doctor captures to disk for those minutes and then builds the package.

While the package is being built, Esc closes the window and the work continues. When it finishes, the window shows the path and the SHA-256; y copies the path and ⏎ or Esc close. The latest evidence stays visible in 7 Capture › Evidence.

How to build the package for support

  1. Press e with the IP selected.
  2. In step 1 check the IP, the window (by default, the last 15 minutes) and the exporters.
  3. In step 2 choose the pcap mode and confirm the rest of the checkboxes.
  4. In step 3 decide whether to pseudonymize third parties in the CSV/JSON.
  5. In step 4 press ⏎ and wait for "Package ready".

Expected result: a path like /var/tmp/fl-doctor/fl-doctor-evidence-flowlink-lab-01-20261016-131717.tgz (name of the host and date and time of the build), its SHA-256 and the copy command. The package contains:

  • README.txt, summary.es.txt, summary.en.txt (summaries in Spanish and English with the checks and technical data), summary.json, manifest.json (each file with its sum) and SHA256SUMS;
  • exporters.csv, top-ips.csv, templates.json and ips/ (summary and per-IP records, in CSV and/or JSON);
  • capture/ with the pcap (original.pcap, trimmed.pcapng, trim.json);
  • flowlink/ with the configuration without secrets (config.redacted.yaml), the log excerpt, the cycles (cycles.csv), the new IPs and the pending batches;
  • host/ (system, interfaces, UDP counters, firewall, clock), pce-path.txt and support-context.json.

Wizard field by field

The title of the window always says the step (Evidence · step 2 of 4) and its last line lists the keys. The field with the focus is marked with ▶.

Step 1 · What

FieldHow it works
IPsText. It starts with the IP you had selected (or the watched ones, up to 64). Accepts IPs, CIDR networks, ranges and list:name, separated by commas. Full text-editing keys and pasting work. If something is wrong, PgDn/⏎ shows "«999.1.1.1» is not a valid IP, network, range or list" and does not advance.
Window← → (or Space) change between "since fl-doctor opened", "last" and "a new capture of".
MinutesOnly for "last" and "a new capture of". ← → ±5; or type digits (+ - also work). Maximum 1,440 for "last" and 60 for a new capture.
ExportersOne checkbox per exporter seen (up to 64, each IP once). Space marks. With none marked, all are included ("Unmarked: all the exporters are included.").

How to build the package for one IP and one exporter only

  1. Select the IP on any tab and press e.
  2. Tab to the Exporters list, move to the switch you want and press Space ([✓]).
  3. PgDn for step 2.

How to capture new traffic instead of using what is already stored

  1. In Window, press → until it says "a new capture of".
  2. In Minutes, set how long to capture (up to 60) and continue with PgDn.

Expected result: when you confirm, fl-doctor captures to disk for those minutes and then builds the package (the window says "Building the package…" and tells you that Esc closes it while the work continues).

How to fix an invalid IP in step 1

If you press PgDn with a wrong text, a red line explains what failed and the focus stays in the field. Correct it (Ctrl-U erases everything) and continue.

Step 2 · Contents

Seven lines, each with a symbol or a value in brackets:

LineValues
Summary and chain statusAlways included (✓ … (always)).
evidence pcapno pcap, original, trimmed, original and trimmed. ← → or Space cycle.
decoded records per IPno records, CSV, JSON, CSV and JSON.
FlowLink log excerpts[✓] / [ ] with Space.
configuration without secrets[✓] / [ ].
host state[✓] / [ ].
exit to the PCE (DNS, proxy, TLS)[✓] / [ ].

Under the lines: "Estimated total size: ≈ …" (each line with a pcap or records shows its own estimate) and, when the pcap is original, the warning "The original pcap carries third-party records (those sharing a datagram)." Over 200 MB it adds "The package exceeds 200 MB: it is better to choose the trimmed pcap or drop the records."

Step 3 · Privacy

One checkbox (Space): "Pseudonymize in CSV/JSON the IPs that are not of interest". Marked, the third-party IPs of the CSV and JSON files are replaced; the original pcap is never altered (hence the warning in the step if you chose it).

Step 4 · Confirm

The summary repeats IPs, window, contents, estimated size (≈ 3.2 MB (≤ 200 MB)) and the path, and prints the equivalent command; the line Build the package (⏎) is selected. ⏎ builds it.

While it builds and when it finishes

Esc closes the window and the work continues in the background. When the package is ready, a window shows ✓ Package ready, the Path, the SHA-256, the Size, any notices (for example that there was no disk capture, so the pcap could not be included) and the equivalent command. y copies the path; ⏎ or Esc close. The same notice stays in the message history (M).

Note: Step 4 and the "Package ready" window show the same equivalent command, written with the English names the command line uses (--last 15m, --pcap both, and list:<name> for a watch list); you can copy it as is into your own scripts. When your choices cannot be written as a command (contents, exporters, pseudonymization), step 4 adds "Approximate equivalent: the command line uses the default contents and does not filter exporters".

Pcap modes

ModeWhat it containsWhen to use it
original (default)The complete datagrams that contain the IP, plus their templates. It opens in Wireshark with no extra steps.Support needs to see the datagrams as they arrived. It includes records of other IPs that traveled in the same datagram.
trimmedDatagrams rebuilt with only the records of interest.When third-party data must not be shared.
original and trimmed (both)Both.To choose later what to share.
no pcapNo pcap.Only the summary and records are needed.

The pcap comes from disk: from the disk capture you asked for (C), from the black box if it is on, or from the file being analyzed (--file). fl-doctor does not keep packets in memory "just in case". If there is nothing on disk, the package comes out without a pcap and says how to get one. With evidence --ip … (command line), the command starts the disk capture before observing. The package has a size cap (200 MB by default, 1,024 MB at most); if the pcap does not fit, it is trimmed and the package says so.

Disk capture

C on an IP (in Seen, Flows, IPs or Home) offers to capture its traffic to disk. The window shows the IPs and the cap (1.0 GB by default; change it in Settings › Memory & statistics) and reminds you that nothing is stored until you accept. ⏎ (or y/s) starts; Esc (or n) cancels. fl-doctor launches tcpdump or dumpcap in a ring of files with the total cap (the oldest is overwritten), with the filter for the collector's flow ports, in a private subfolder of /var/tmp/fl-doctor/capturas/. The header shows rec ● used/cap and C again stops it. The files stay on disk to build the evidence.

Note: If memory is at attention or critical level, the capture window warns you: new evidence opens only with your confirmation.

Dedicated capture and Keep running after exit

c opens a form to launch tcpdump or dumpcap to disk with its ring and caps (Tab/↑ ↓ change field, ← → or Space change the value, ⏎ starts, Esc cancels):

FieldWhat it is
Tooltcpdump or dumpcap (the installed and most used one comes first).
InterfacesInterfaces, comma-separated; empty = all.
BPF filterA BPF filter by hand; empty = the one generated for FlowLink's ports.
Maximum durationMinutes, up to 240 (4 h). With the checkbox below on, up to 1,440 (24 h).
Ring files / MB per fileThe ring (10 files of 100 MB by default).
Keep running after exitCheckbox, off by default.

By default the capture dies with fl-doctor: it leaves no root processes running. With Keep running after exit on, the capture can keep going after you close fl-doctor, up to its duration cap, which with the checkbox rises to 24 hours at most (the process ends by itself when it gets there: it is never left without a limit). On exit, the confirmation warns that captures are still running and, with the terminal already restored, fl-doctor prints for each one:

fl-doctor: a disk capture was left running (tcpdump), as chosen when it was started.
  pid: 4242
  it stops by itself in 3 h 59 min (limit 4 h; the maximum is 24 h)
  files: /var/tmp/fl-doctor/capturas/…
  to stop it: sudo pkill -TERM -f /var/tmp/fl-doctor/capturas/…

The captures' disk budget (2 GiB) counts what is committed: every capture that is still alive, from this run or an earlier one, reserves its whole ring even if it has written little so far.

Black box

--blackbox 200M (from 16 MiB to 4 GiB; also in Settings › Memory & statistics) keeps the last minutes of the collector's traffic on disk with that cap. It is off by default. It restarts itself, is deleted when you turn it off or exit, and only exists with live capture. It is useful for building evidence of something that already happened without having asked for the capture beforehand.

Where the package ends up and how to copy it

The .tgz is left in /var/tmp/fl-doctor/ (a private root folder, permissions 0700), with permissions 600 and next to its .sha256. Since the folder belongs to root, whoever logged in with sudo cannot read the file without copying it. When finished, fl-doctor prints the exact command, in this form:

sudo install -m 0600 -o <your_user> -- /var/tmp/fl-doctor/<package>.tgz /var/tmp/fl-doctor/<package>.tgz.sha256 ~/

If it finds an output folder that is not yours or that allows writes by others, it rejects it and says what to do, without touching anything: it asks for a new folder of your own with --output (for example sudo mkdir -m 700 /var/tmp/fl-doctor-NEW). It never suggests chown or chmod on a folder that may be shared (/tmp, a HOME). There are no automatic copies: you decide what leaves the host.

Reading a package (fl-doctor read)

fl-doctor read <package>.tgz opens the package (in the interface if there is a terminal; otherwise it prints a summary), verifies each file's SHA-256 sum and shows the chain state. If the sums do not match, it says so ("the package is damaged or was modified") and exits with code 2. It also opens packages that support repacked (tar czf x.tgz -C folder .) and those from earlier versions; it rejects paths that leave the package (.., absolute), links and devices. Review the content before sending it.

Headless use (CLI)

Same engine as the interface, with text output, --json (versioned schema) or --csv. With no subcommand and no terminal, fl-doctor does not open the interface: it says "stdout is not a terminal; use a subcommand" and exits with code 3.

Common options

They apply to all subcommands and to the interface.

OptionWhat it does
--jsonJSON output with a versioned schema.
--no-inputNever asks; if an answer is needed, it fails.
--offlineDoes not test the exit to the PCE (D1–D4).
--profile FILESite profile (replaces /etc/fl-doctor/site.toml).
--portablePreferences and state in ./fl-doctor-datos/.
`--engine auto\native\tcpdump\dumpcap`Capture engine (FLDOCTOR_ENGINE).
`--lang es\en`Language of the help, interface and messages (FLDOCTOR_LANG).
`--theme auto\brand\terminal\light\mono`Interface theme.
--output DIROutput folder for captures and evidence (FLDOCTOR_OUTPUT).
--patterns FILELog pattern catalog that replaces the embedded one.
--interface IF[,IF]Capture interfaces (default: those with an IP).
`--ports flowlink\udp\all\6500,2055`Capture ports: FlowLink's, all UDP, UDP and TCP, or a list (1 to 64 ports).
--exporter IP[,IP]Only those exporters.
--filter '…'Global filter in the filter language. In top it is the ranking's filter.
--observe NSeconds to observe before judging (default 20; 0 = no capture).
--file capture.pcapAnalyze a .pcap/.pcapng instead of capturing live.
--config config.yamlUse that FlowLink config.yaml instead of the host's (analyze a pcap on another machine).
--flowlink-exe PATH, `--flowlink-user USER\UID`Declare the binary and the account of a FlowLink started by hand or installed outside the package paths (repeatable; also in site.toml).
`--memory lean\normal\large`Memory profile.
--blackbox 200MBlack box with that cap (16 MiB to 4 GiB).
--window MINStatistics window in minutes (1 to 120; the maximum depends on the profile).
-h, --help, -V, --versionHelp and version.
Important: Declaring a process with --flowlink-exe or --flowlink-user gives it authority over which files fl-doctor reads (it runs as root and opens the --config and --log-file that process names). Declare only what the administrator installed; fl-doctor does not build a ready-to-copy option if the executable is in a place another user can modify.

health

Checks A–D and log indicators. It observes 20 seconds of traffic by default.

  • --log-only: evaluates only the monitoring indicators (L01, L04, L06, L07, L10, L11, L12, L13 and L15), without capturing (0 s). Meant for continuous monitoring.
  • With --file, it judges on that pcap. 
sudo fl-doctor health
sudo fl-doctor health --log-only --no-input

trace

Evidence ladder N0–N4 per IP.

  • --ip IP[,IP] (required, up to 256 IPs).
  • --last 1m|5m|15m|1h (default 15m): which part of the statistics is shown. It is not the memory --window. 
sudo fl-doctor trace --ip 198.51.100.20 --observe 300

top

Ranking of IPs, networks or exporters.

  • --by ip|net24|exporter (default ip), --n N (default 50; the ranking keeps 1,000 at most and warns on stderr if you ask for more), --last 1m|5m|15m|1h, --csv.
  • --filter replaces the ranking's default filter (class private). 
sudo fl-doctor top --n 20 --observe 120
sudo fl-doctor top --by exporter --observe 120 --csv

log

Summary of cycles, responses, errors, discards and new IPs in the log, without capturing traffic.

  • --since WHEN: 90s, 15m, 2h, 1d (backwards from now) or an RFC 3339 time (2026-10-13T14:00:00Z). 
sudo fl-doctor log --since 2h

If the log has rotated history (flowlink.log.N[.gz]), it reads it from newest to oldest with a 90-second deadline; the subcommand waits up to about 100 s.

evidence

Builds the evidence package; prints the path, SHA-256, size and equivalent command.

  • --ip IP|NET|RANGE|list:NAME[,…] (required). list:NAME (alias lista:NAME) expands to the elements of a saved watch list (watchlist.toml or the site profile), so the equivalent command written by the wizard can be pasted as is; a list that does not exist is a usage error. trace and commands take plain IPs only.
  • --last 1m|5m|15m|1h (default 15m).
  • --pcap original|trimmed|both (default original). 
sudo fl-doctor evidence --ip 198.51.100.20 --last 15m --pcap both

read

Analyzes a .pcap/.pcapng or opens an evidence package (.tgz).

fl-doctor read capture.pcap
fl-doctor read fl-doctor-evidence-colector-01-20261005-142000.tgz
fl-doctor top --file capture.pcap --config config.yaml       # on another machine

Large files are read in two passes: the first gathers the templates (like tshark -2) and the second reads the records. A file of several GB takes twice as long before giving figures; meanwhile the interface says "pass 1/2" and then "pass 2/2", with the figures marked as partial until the end.

commands

Prints the tcpdump, dumpcap and tshark commands for the installed version, with the collector's ports. --ip IP[,IP] is optional.

fl-doctor commands --ip 198.51.100.20

demo, doctor and selftest

  • demo: the interface with synthetic exporters (no network or root). Without a terminal it prints the screens as text (--observe N seconds, 6 by default).
  • doctor: diagnostics of the terminal (size, UTF-8, color, OSC 11, OSC 52, glyphs) and of the preference paths.
  • selftest: platform test with no network or FlowLink (needs root). --output DIR chooses where to leave the .json and the .tgz.

Output, schema and exit codes

  • Text, JSON or CSV. --json gives a versioned schema; top --csv is for spreadsheets (rank,key,ip,name,watched,flows,percent,approximate,error_bound,bytes,packets,as_source,as_destination,peers,main_exporter,main_exporter_name,extra_exporters; empty error_bound = exact).
  • Final line. Every run ends with a FL-DOCTOR-RESULT key=value … line. With --json or --csv that line goes to stderr, so it does not break the JSON or CSV.
  • Schema 2. The line starts with schema=2 version=… command=… code=…; command is always the English name. Each JSON carries "schema": "fl-doctor.<command>/2" (for example fl-doctor.health/2). Whoever reads the line or the JSON must check schema. There is no compatibility mode for schema 1 (Spanish keys).
  • Keys per command. status (ok, warning, failure, info, no_data), failures, warnings, observed_s, host (health); status, ips, with_trail, observed_s (trace); rows, records, observed_s and row_limit (top); status, cycles, bad_data (log); package, sha256, bytes, observed_s (evidence); datagrams, records, malformed, exporters (read of a pcap) and sums_ok, status (read of a package); commands; utf8, color, size_ok (doctor); result, checks, failures, budget_mb (selftest). 
FL-DOCTOR-RESULT schema=2 version=0.1.0 command=health code=1 status=warning failures=0 warnings=2 observed_s=20 host=colector-01
CodeMeaning
0OK
1Warning
2Failure
3Incorrect usage (arguments, missing file, no terminal)
4Missing permissions (capture or log without root)

If the process receives a stop signal (kill, SSH drop), it restores the terminal and exits with 128 plus the signal number.

Note: The previous version's names (salud, rastrear, evidencia, leer, comandos, autoprueba, --observar, --archivo, --salida, --sin-red…) still work as hidden aliases, with no retirement date: they do not appear in --help, but an old script does not break. The same goes for the variables FLDOCTOR_SALIDA, FLDOCTOR_MOTOR, FLDOCTOR_SITIO and FLDOCTOR_PORTATIL.

Examples and cron

Quick recipes:

sudo fl-doctor health
sudo fl-doctor top --by exporter --observe 120
sudo fl-doctor trace --ip 198.51.100.20 --observe 300
sudo fl-doctor log --since 2h
fl-doctor commands --ip 198.51.100.20
fl-doctor top --file capture.pcap --config config.yaml       # on another machine

Monitoring with cron every 10 minutes (the exit code and the FL-DOCTOR-RESULT line end up in the log):

*/10 * * * * root /usr/local/bin/fl-doctor health --log-only --no-input >> /var/log/fl-doctor-health.log 2>&1

Memory and performance

How it works

fl-doctor does not store packets: it reads each datagram once, updates counters and drops it. What matters are the counts kept over time: which IPs it saw, which ones FlowLink reports and through which exporter they arrive. That is why its memory reaches a plateau and does not grow with the flow volume.

Totals, exporters, watched IPs and log indicators are exact. What does not fit is approximated and marked (≈).

Profiles and effective cap

--memory lean|normal|large (default normal), or the profile in Settings › Memory & statistics:

ProfileBudgetStatistics window (default / maximum)Live rowsMeasured
lean32 MiB30 / 30 min500≈ 14 MB
normal (default)64 MiB30 / 60 min2,000≈ 22 MB (startup peak ≈ 33 MB)
large256 MiB30 / 120 min2,000—

The measurements are from a Rocky 9 x86_64 virtual machine with a real capture replayed for 5 minutes, flat over time. The normal profile has a brief peak (under a second, about 10 to 12 MB above the plateau) shortly after startup, when the first full host reading happens with traffic already flowing; it goes back to the plateau and stays inside the 64 MiB budget.

The effective cap is the lowest of the profile, 80% of the cgroup memory limit and 5% of the host's RAM (the latter with a 32 MiB floor). fl-doctor shrinks before bothering FlowLink and says so (in Host › Resources: "profile normal", "limited by the cgroup (80 %)" or "limited by the RAM (5 %)").

The budget is split across components (MiB):

Profilebasecapturedecoderankingexportersliveevidenceinventoryheadroom
lean1244331221
normal1588862467
large20404060308162418

Indicator and levels

The header shows mem ● 41/64 MB · system 2.1 GB free · window 30m: what fl-doctor uses against its budget, the host's available memory and the statistics window. The symbol changes with the level and does not rely on color alone:

LevelSymbolWhenWhat fl-doctor does
Normal●Below the thresholdsNothing special.
Attention▲Own use > 80% of the budget, host with < 20% available memory, PSI some pressure or cgroup > 80%Lowers the resolution of optional items and asks for confirmation before opening new evidence. The indicator is no longer trimmed.
Critical✗Own use > 95%, < 10% available, PSI full or cgroup > 95%Closes Live and counts 1 of every N unwatched records (sampled 1:N).

A level is entered when the condition holds for 3 seconds and left when it drops with a margin for 10 seconds. Red is reserved for when the collector is at risk (low host memory, PSI pressure or cgroup); if only fl-doctor reached its own budget, the notice says "the collector is not at risk". The detail (VmHWM peak, private memory, component by component, cgroup, pressure, kernel and fl-doctor discards) is in 6 Host › Resources.

Statistics window

--window MINUTES (30 by default; 1 to 120, up to the profile's maximum) is how long the counts and the inventory of IPs seen are kept. The screen window (t: 1m, 5m, 15m, 1h) chooses which part is shown and never exceeds the statistics window. To widen it to 90 minutes you need the large profile.

Settings › Memory & statistics menu

S (or "Settings · Memory & statistics" in the palette) opens the menu. ↑ ↓ choose the row, ← → (or -, +, Space) change the value, d goes back to the chosen profile's defaults, ⏎ applies on the fly and saves to config.toml ([memoria] section), and Esc cancels.

RowValues
Profilelean, normal, large
Stats window1, 5, 10, 15, 30, 45, 60, 90 or 120 min (up to the profile's maximum)
Black boxoff, 16 MiB, 64 MiB, 256 MiB, 1 GiB or 4 GiB
Disk capture cap64 MiB, 256 MiB, 1 GiB (default), 2 GiB, 4 GiB or 16 GiB
Auto samplingyes (default) or no

Below you can see the resulting budget ("Budget 64 MB · profile normal · exact inventory up to N IPs"). Command-line parameters take precedence over preferences.

How to change the memory profile

  1. Press S.
  2. With ↓ go to Profile and change with → to lean or large; the window row is clamped to the new profile's maximum.
  3. Press ⏎.

Expected result: a notice "Applied: profile lean · stats window 30 min · saved in config.toml." and the new budget in the header. The equivalent command line is fl-doctor --memory lean --window 30.

Sampling under pressure

With Auto sampling on, at critical level fl-doctor counts 1 of every N unwatched records, with the counters scaled ×N and marked approximate. Watched IPs, exporters and log indicators are never sampled, and neither is anything when analyzing a file (--file): the result has to be complete.

Preferences and site profile

Files and precedence

fl-doctor remembers the theme, language, window, columns, filters and watched IPs. It never stores secrets.

FileContent
~/.config/fl-doctor/config.tomlTheme, language, color, glyphs, refresh, bar, mouse, capture, evidence and memory.
~/.config/fl-doctor/watchlist.tomlNamed IP lists and which one is active.
~/.config/fl-doctor/filters.tomlSaved filters.
~/.local/state/fl-doctor/state.tomlDisposable state: last tab and focus, window, columns and order, bookmarks, tour seen. If corrupt it is renamed to state.toml.corrupto and starts from scratch.
~/.local/state/fl-doctor/historial.jsonlCommands, filters and tools used (up to 1,000, with a secrets filter).
/etc/fl-doctor/site.tomlSite profile: expected exporters and networks, trusted FlowLink. Placed by the administrator; fl-doctor does not write it.

Precedence: command-line parameters > FLDOCTOR_* variables > portable mode > the user's preferences > site.toml > defaults.

With sudo, the folders of the user who invoked it (SUDO_USER) are used and files are created with that owner; if that cannot be resolved, preferences become read-only with a warning and last only for that session.

config.toml

The key names are the file's own, today in Spanish. Only what you change is saved; unknown keys produce a warning, never an error.

version = 1
[ui]
tema = "auto"        # auto | marca | terminal | claro | mono
idioma = "es"        # es | en
color = "auto"       # auto | 16 | 256 | truecolor | no
glifos = "unicode"   # unicode | bloques | ascii
refresco_ms = 1000   # 100 | 250 | 500 | 1000 | 2000 | 5000
barra = "completa"   # completa | minima
mouse = false
[captura]
motor = "auto"       # auto | nativo | tcpdump | dumpcap
anillo = { archivos = 10, mb = 100, minutos = 60 }
[evidencia]
pcap = "original"    # original | recortado | ambos
salida = "/var/tmp/fl-doctor"
[memoria]
perfil = "normal"    # lean | normal | large
ventana_min = 30
caja_negra_mb = 0    # 0 = off
captura_disco_tope_mb = 1024
muestreo_auto = true

site.toml

The site profile carries what the operator would expect to see. Everything is optional; without a profile, fl-doctor discovers what it can. Limited to 1 MiB.

version = 1
puertos = [2055, 6500]      # flow ports in addition to the YAML's
color = "truecolor"         # forces color (PuTTY supports it but does not announce it)
flowlink_exe = ["/opt/sitio/bin/flowlink"]   # same as --flowlink-exe
flowlink_user = ["opsflow", "1001"]          # same as --flowlink-user

[rutas]                     # only if they are not the defaults
config = "/etc/illumio-flowlink/config.yaml"
log = "/var/log/illumio-flowlink/flowlink.log"
datos = "/var/lib/illumio-flowlink/data"

[[exportadores]]            # expected exporters (check A1)
ip = "192.0.2.11"
nombre = "sw-core-01"

[[redes]]                   # networks whose IPs are expected ("expected" filter)
red = "198.51.100.0/24"
nombre = "servidores"

[[vigiladas]]               # preloaded IPs (the "perfil" list)
nombre = "dns-01"
objetivo = "198.51.100.20"

A process is accepted as FlowLink by its exact executable, never by its name. By default only the package's (/usr/local/bin, /usr/bin, /usr/sbin, /usr/local/illumio, /opt/illumio-flowlink), root's or the service user's are accepted.

watchlist.toml and filters.toml

watchlist.toml stores lista_activa and one or more lists with their elements (nombre, objetivo and optional etiquetas); the interface writes it when you watch or stop watching. filters.toml stores the named filters (nombre, texto, vista, fecha; up to 200). Both can be edited by hand.

Earlier names and portable mode

  • Earlier names. Earlier versions called these files vigiladas.toml, filtros.toml and sitio.toml. On startup, fl-doctor moves vigiladas.toml and filtros.toml to the new name atomically and without following symbolic links (a link with the old name is not migrated: it warns and leaves it as it was; if the new name already exists, the new one wins). The site profile, which fl-doctor does not write, is read under the old name if the new one is missing, with a warning that you should rename it.
  • Portable mode. --portable (or an fl-doctor.toml next to the binary) stores everything in ./fl-doctor-datos/. As root it only applies if the folder belongs to root and does not allow writes by others.

Environment variables

VariableEquivalent to
FLDOCTOR_LANG--lang
FLDOCTOR_ENGINE--engine
FLDOCTOR_OUTPUT--output
FLDOCTOR_CONFIG_DIR, FLDOCTOR_STATE_DIR, FLDOCTOR_CACHE_DIRPreferences, state and cache folders.
FLDOCTOR_SITEPath of the site profile.
FLDOCTOR_PORTABLEPortable mode.
NO_COLOR=1Removes color.

When running as root, the FLDOCTOR_* variables that point to paths only apply if the path belongs to root and nobody else can write to it (so sudo -E or an env_keep do not let an unprivileged user's environment through); what is ignored is reported. An --output typed on the command line is respected.

Troubleshooting and limits

Common problems

SymptomWhat to do
"Enlarge the terminal: minimum 80×24, now …"The terminal needs 80×24 at least.
Odd or square symbolsRun fl-doctor doctor; in Settings (,) set Glyphs = ascii.
Native capture does not open (header: capture ✗)Run with sudo, or use --engine tcpdump.
"No datagrams on UDP 6500 for 60 s"Does the switch point at the collector's right IP? Does the firewall let the traffic through (tab 6)? Does it arrive at another port (tab 2 shows every port seen)?
The IP does not appear (N0)Check the switch's sampling (tab 2), observe longer and confirm its traffic goes through the exporting device.
v9/IPFIX records not decodedTemplates are missing: the exporter resends them every so often. Wait for them to arrive, or capture from before the exporter restarted.
The ranking shows ≈It is an upper bound of the approximate ranking. Watch the IP with Space for its exact count.
Seen shows ? unknownreported_ips.dat was not read, is not recognized or was read incompletely: "not reported" cannot be claimed. Check permissions and run with sudo.
health exits with code 4Missing permissions to see everything (capture or log). Run with sudo and the full path of the binary.
Indicators say "The history of the rotated logs is still being read"The log exists; fl-doctor reads the flowlink.log.N[.gz] files with a 90 s deadline. Subcommands wait up to about 100 s; if that is not enough, repeat in a while. You do not need to change the path or use root.
FlowLink shows as "not visible"It runs in a non-standard way: use --flowlink-exe or --flowlink-user (or flowlink_exe / flowlink_user in site.toml). Declare only a root-owned executable.
fl-doctor rejects the output folder (not yours or writable by others)Give a new folder of your own with --output; fl-doctor does not write to shared folders such as /tmp.
The package comes out without a pcapThere was nothing on disk. Ask for a disk capture (C), turn on the black box or use evidence --ip …, which starts the capture before observing.
Copy does not reach the clipboardThe terminal does not support OSC 52: Y saves to a file.
A key does nothingLook at the footer of the window or at the help (?): the keys depend on the screen and on the focused panel (Tab). In a text box only editing keys apply; Esc closes it.
Esc does not quitBy design: Esc only closes what you opened. Quit with q or Ctrl-C.
The + key adds an IP instead of zooming the windowOn 3 IPs + adds an IP and t copies the tshark command; zoom the window with - or use the palette ("Time window: …").
A filter applied before "disappeared"Filters have three scopes (global with F, the ranking's own and the IPs list). Open / and F to see which one holds it; chips show every active term.
Table columns are missingThey are hidden by priority when the terminal is narrow (Shift-→ slides the table), or they are optional ones that you add from the palette ("Exporters: show the … column").
The capture to disk does not start ("The capture could not be started")The output folder must exist and belong to you or root, and tcpdump or dumpcap must be installed. Check the message in M and run fl-doctor with sudo.
sampled 1:N appears in the headerMemory at critical level. Watched IPs, exporters and indicators are not sampled. See "Memory and performance".
selftest failsIt must run as root. The disk-capture check needs tcpdump or dumpcap. Send back the .tgz it leaves.

Known limits of 0.1

  • Tested on Rocky 9 and UBI 8 (arm64) and, with the self-test, on Rocky 9 x86_64. It still has to be validated on a real Illumio FlowLink user's collector. RHEL 7 (kernel 3.10) is not verified: AF_PACKET with PACKET_IGNORE_OUTGOING falls back to the packet-type filter and the new fragments filter was not run there.
  • The dumpcap engine is not verified against an abrupt death (SIGKILL) of fl-doctor in the middle of a capture; with tcpdump it is.
  • The format of FlowLink's text consumer is an assumption: it still has to be checked against a real configuration.
  • Times are shown in UTC.
  • The generated BPF filter covers IPv4 fragments. Also, BPF cannot filter by the IPs inside the records: use tshark afterwards.
  • An unwatched IP shows a main exporter in the ranking; the breakdown by port, service and peers exists only for watched IPs.
  • A record's extra fields keep up to 16 bytes of value (the rest is cut and marked); the field name is not kept in Live.
  • If an exporter restarts with a different definition for the same template id, its records are decoded wrongly until it resends the template.
  • The "bad data" discards in a telco project were 100% ICMP: that is a field observation, not a rule documented by Illumio.
  • The release is not signed: verify it against the SHA-256 sums.
  • A few texts still come out in Spanish with --lang en: the usage errors that are checked before the language is known (an invalid size, window or port list, "«x» no es una dirección IP" and "indique entre 1 y 256 IPs" in trace, an invalid duration in log --since), the prefix of the error for an unreadable --config, the notice "the configuration file does not exist" and, outside Linux, the notice that AF_PACKET does not exist. Conversely, with --lang es a few status labels of the Exporters tab stay in English ("accepts", "no listener", "not in remote_addrs", "resend every N s", "no sampling"). Names that are written or stored also stay in Spanish for now: the plantillas/ folder of the cache, the glifos key of config.toml (the one doctor quotes) and the similar-subcommand suggestions of the argument parser. They do not change what the tool does.
  • The history of rotated logs (flowlink.log.N[.gz]) is not read continuously: it can skip some of the middle files. The indicators that depend on it say so while it is being read.
  • The tab 7 Capture does not list the disk capture of one IP started with C; that capture shows only in the header (rec ●) and in 6 Host. Dedicated captures (c) are listed.
  • The hexadecimal view (x) of a Live record changes only the template fields; records without template fields look the same.
  • A watched network or range cannot be selected or removed from the interface; edit watchlist.toml to remove it.
  • Unofficial tool, provided "as is", with no Illumio support.

Where everything else comes from

What describes how fl-doctor works (N0–N4 ladder, memory, evidence, keys) comes from its own manual and the version 0.1.0 code, not from FlowLink's documentation. The memory figures were measured on a Rocky 9 x86_64 virtual machine with a real NetStream capture replayed for 5 minutes. Field observations (for example, that the "bad data" discards were ICMP) are project observations, not product rules.

fl-doctor is not an Illumio product and is not supported by Illumio; it is provided “as is”, without warranty. Screenshot data is synthetic.
